title: saveBody raises a false 'changed outside Fragments' conflict when a second write for the same path is queued with the same expectedBody snapshot
description:
## Summary

`FragmentLibrary.saveBody` performs an optimistic-concurrency check by comparing the file's
current body against an `expectedBody` snapshot supplied by the caller. When two writes for the
*same path* are issued back-to-back with the *same* snapshot, the second one falsely reports that
the note "changed outside Fragments" — even though **Fragments itself** performed the first write
and no external edit ever occurred.

The plugin's own draft-flush path triggers exactly this: the unmount/selection-change cleanup
passes the snapshot it captured *before* an in-flight autosave had resolved.

## Root cause

`saveBody` validates, then writes, inside a per-path serialized queue:

```ts
// src/library.ts
async saveBody(path: string, body: string, expectedBody?: string): Promise<void> {
  await this.queue(path, async () => {
    const file = this.file(path);
    await run(() =>
      this.app.vault.process(file, (source) => {
        if (expectedBody !== undefined && bodyOf(source) !== expectedBody) {
          throw new Error(
            "This note changed outside Fragments. Copy your draft, then reopen the note before saving.",
          );
        }
        ...
```

```ts
private async queue(path: string, operation: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {
  const previous = this.pending.get(path) ?? Promise.resolve();
  const current = previous.catch(() => undefined).then(operation);   // <-- deferred
  this.pending.set(path, current);
  ...
}
```

`queue` **defers** the operation onto the previous promise for that path. `expectedBody` was
captured by the caller *before* the deferral, so by the time the second operation actually runs,
the first one has already mutated the file. The comparison then sees its own prior write and
declares a conflict.

There is no external editor, no sync client and no second Obsidian window involved.

## Trigger

In `useDraft` (`src/app.tsx`) `savedBody.current` is only advanced in the autosave's `.then`:

```ts
void library.saveBody(selected, draft, body).then(() => {
  savedBody.current = draft;          // runs AFTER the write resolves
  ...
});
```

while the selection-change / unmount cleanup reads it synchronously:

```ts
useEffect(() => () => {
  const writing = pendingDraft.current;
  if (writing?.path === selected)
    void library.saveBody(writing.path, writing.text, savedBody.current).catch(errorNotice);
}, [selected, library]);
```

So if the user switches fragments (or closes the window) while the 700 ms autosave is still in
flight, the flush passes the pre-autosave snapshot and collides with the autosave queued ahead of it.

## Impact

- The user is told to "Copy your draft, then reopen the note before saving" for a conflict that
  Fragments manufactured against itself. That is actively misleading: it invites the user to
  believe their work is at risk when the file on disk already holds their latest text.
- The draft is not lost (call #1 already persisted it), but the user has no way to know that, and
  the error is indistinguishable from a genuine external-edit conflict.
- This directly undermines the README guarantee: *"Fragments reads changes made to the Markdown
  files outside the app and avoids overwriting a note changed while a draft was open."* The check
  fires on changes Fragments made itself, so it is not a reliable signal.

## Reproduction

The real `src/library.ts` bundled with esbuild (`obsidian` aliased to a faithful stub of
`getFrontMatterInfo` / `normalizePath` / `TFile` and an in-memory vault that yields on `process`,
standing in for a real disk), then two plain calls. No React involved.

```js
const expected = await lib.read("Fragments/A.md");        // "\nORIGINAL\n"
const autosave  = lib.saveBody("Fragments/A.md", "DRAFT 1", expected);
const flush     = lib.saveBody("Fragments/A.md", "DRAFT 1", expected);
await autosave; await flush;
```

Output:

```
savedBody snapshot passed by BOTH calls: "\nORIGINAL\n"
  [process] expectedBody check passed, wrote "DRAFT 1"
call#1 autosave: OK
  [process] REJECTED: This note changed outside Fragments. Copy your draft, then reopen the note before saving.
call#2 unmount-flush: THREW (see [process] above)
final disk body: "DRAFT 1"
=> both calls wrote the SAME text; no external edit ever happened: true
```

The file ends up with the intended text, yet call #2 reported a conflict.

## Suggested fix

Make the concurrency check re-validate against the value that is actually current for the path at
the moment the queued operation runs, instead of a caller snapshot that may predate a queued
write. For example, track the last body the library itself wrote per path and treat a match against
that as current:

```ts
// treat a body this library just wrote as equivalent to the caller's snapshot
private readonly written = new Map<string, string>();
```

or, more simply, have the app's cleanup flush read `savedBody.current` *inside* the promise chain
rather than at call time, and/or make `saveBody` tolerate a mismatch whose value equals the text it
itself last persisted.

## Relationship to existing issues

- `fragments-tmf` is about the *message*: `run()` collapses the thrown `Error` into
  "An unknown error occurred in Effect.tryPromise". This issue is about the conflict being
  **falsely raised in the first place** — the check is wrong, not the plumbing. Fixing `run`
  would only make the false message legible; it would not stop the false conflict.
- `fragments-nzo` is a `useDraft` state-hygiene bug triggered by a no-match search nulling the
  selection, where `body` is clobbered to `""`. This issue reproduces with no React at all, purely
  at the `saveBody`/`queue` layer, and is independent of which snapshot value is wrong.
- `fragments-tti` is about `trash` omitting the draft flush. This issue is about the flush that
  *does* run being validated against a stale snapshot.
close_reason: saveBody now treats the body it last persisted for a path as current, so a queued second write with a pre-write snapshot no longer reports a self-inflicted external-edit conflict

title: Fragments folder setting is matched case-sensitively and never validated, so re-entering a folder with different case silently shadows the whole library
description:
## Summary

The **Fragments folder** setting is matched **case-sensitively** and is never validated to exist.
Re-entering an existing folder with different capitalisation silently empties the whole library — no
error, no notice — and the next "New Snippet" then creates a *second, shadowing* folder so the user's
real fragments stay invisible and unreachable through the UI.

## Affected code

`src/library.ts` — `contains()` and `changeFolder()`:

```ts
contains = (path: string): boolean => {
  const folder = this.folder();
  return (
    path.startsWith(`${folder}/`) &&          // <-- case-sensitive prefix match
    path.endsWith(".md") &&
    path !== `${folder}/${SCRATCHPAD_NAME}`
  );
};

async changeFolder(folder: string): Promise<void> {
  this.settings.folder = cleanFolder(folder) || "Fragments";   // cleanFolder does NOT resolve case
  await this.load();                                            // no existence check
}
```

`cleanFolder` only trims and normalises separators; it never canonicalises the case against the
vault. `changeFolder` performs no existence check, so a path that matches nothing simply yields an
empty index. The setting is then persisted by `FragmentsSettingTab.updateFolder` → `saveSettings()`.

Note that `FolderSuggest` makes this easy to hit: `getSuggestions` matches case-**insensitively**
(`folder.path.toLowerCase().startsWith(search)`), so the dropdown happily offers `Fragments` while the
field contains a query typed in any case — and `updateFolder` is wired to the field's `change` event,
so plain typing commits it.

## Reproduction (deterministic)

Vault contains:

- `Fragments/note.md`
- `Fragments/Work/deep.md`

Both are indexed correctly under the default setting. Then re-enter the same folder in lowercase
(the exact value `Fragments` differs from only by case):

```ts
const library = new FragmentLibrary(app, { folder: "Fragments" });
await library.load();
await library.changeFolder("fragments");
```

Observed:

```
entries with 'Fragments': ["Fragments/note.md","Fragments/Work/deep.md"]
contains('Fragments/note.md'): true
contains('fragments/note.md'): false
settings.folder is now: fragments
entries after changeFolder('fragments'): []
collections(): []
vault still holds the originals: ["Fragments/note.md","Fragments/Work/deep.md"]
```

The library is now empty while every fragment is still on disk. The user clicks "Create a fragment"
to fix the empty list:

```
create() -> fragments/Untitled fragment.md
vault now: ["Fragments/note.md","Fragments/Work/deep.md","fragments/Untitled fragment.md"]
library sees: ["fragments/Untitled fragment.md"]
original note still present on disk: true
...but is it listed? false
```

Now two folders exist and the entire pre-existing library is shadowed.

The missing validation is demonstrable on its own — a path that does not exist anywhere in the vault
is accepted without complaint:

```
before: ["Fragments/note.md"]
changeFolder('DoesNotExist') threw: (nothing - silent success)
after: []
collections(): []
```

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** a folder that differs from an existing one only by case is treated as that folder, or
  is rejected with a clear message. A folder path that does not exist should surface an error rather
  than silently emptying the library.
- **Actual:** the case difference is taken at face value, the index silently empties, and the plugin
  then writes new fragments into a duplicate folder that shadows the user's real library.

## Impact

- **Silent data disappearance from the UI.** Every fragment still exists in the vault, but Fragments
  lists none of them. There is no notice and no error to explain it.
- **Shadowing is self-inflicted and compounding.** Because `createCollection` / `create` /
  `ensureFolder` happily create the new path, a user who clicks "New Snippet" to react to the empty
  list gets a duplicate tree. Recovery requires manually finding the original folder and restoring the
  setting by hand.
- The same silent-accept path applies to any typo, so a one-character mistake in the setting
  reproduces the whole scenario.

## Evidence notes

Observed with the real `FragmentLibrary` (`changeFolder`, `create`, `contains`, `load`) driven by a
mock vault implementing the documented Obsidian contracts. The result is independent of frontmatter
parsing, `Effect` scheduling, and React: it is a pure consequence of `contains()` doing
`path.startsWith(`${folder}/`)` against an unvalidated, uncanonicalised setting.

## Suggested fix direction

Canonicalise the requested folder against `vault.getAllFolders()` (case-insensitive match) before
committing it, and reject a folder that does not exist rather than accepting an empty library.
close_reason: changeFolder canonicalises against vault.getAllFolders() case-insensitively and rejects folders that do not exist; load() adopts the vault's casing so the library never silently empties

title: Preview's un-awaited MarkdownRenderer.render clobbers the current fragment: preview shows a previously selected fragment's content
description:
## Summary

The `Preview` component in `src/app.tsx` calls `MarkdownRenderer.render(...)` without awaiting it
and without any cancellation or staleness check. `MarkdownRenderer.render` is asynchronous in
Obsidian (post-processors, embeds, wikilink/codeblock resolution), so it writes into the DOM
*whenever it resolves*, not when it was requested.

If the selected fragment changes while a render is in flight, the earlier render resolves last and
overwrites the newer one. The preview pane then displays **the previously selected fragment's
content** while a different fragment is selected.

## Root cause

```tsx
// src/app.tsx
function Preview({ body, path, view, plugin, language }) {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    const element = ref.current;
    if (!element) return;
    element.empty();
    if (findLanguage(language)?.id === "markdown") {
      void MarkdownRenderer.render(plugin.app, body, element, path, view);   // <-- un-awaited
      return;
    }
    const code = element.createEl("pre").createEl("code");
    highlightCode(code, body, language);
  }, [body, path, view, plugin, language]);
  return <div className="fragments-preview markdown-rendered" ref={ref} />;
}
```

Two problems compound:

1. `void MarkdownRenderer.render(...)` discards the promise, so nothing can sequence or cancel it.
2. There is no `active`/`cancelled` flag in the cleanup (contrast `useDraft`, which does use an
   `active` boolean) and no post-resolution check that `path`/`body` are still current.

`element.empty()` at the top of the next effect run does not help: the stale render performs its
write *after* that `empty()`, so the last write wins by completion time rather than by request time.

Note this only affects the `markdown` branch. The non-markdown branch (`highlightCode`) is
synchronous, so syntax-highlighted previews are unaffected.

## Reproduction

1. Create two markdown fragments, `Alpha` (body `ALPHA_CONTENT`) and `Beta` (body
   `BETA_CONTENT`), both with `language: markdown` in frontmatter.
2. Switch the editor to Preview mode.
3. Select `Alpha`, then quickly select `Beta` before `Alpha`'s render finishes — e.g. with a note
   containing a slow embed/transclusion, or simply by clicking quickly.
4. `Beta`'s render resolves first and is correct; then `Alpha`'s render resolves and overwrites it.

Observed (real `AppShell` + real `FragmentLibrary`, with `MarkdownRenderer.render` made explicitly
async to make the ordering deterministic rather than timing-dependent):

```
in preview mode: true
in-flight jobs - beta: 3 alpha: 2
after Beta renders      : "RENDERED:BETA_CONTENT\n"
selected fragment       : Beta
preview finally shows   : "RENDERED:ALPHA_CONTENT\n"
BUG (shows Alpha)?      : YES - stale render clobbered the current fragment
```

The selected-fragment title still reads `Beta`, so the pane is self-contradictory.

## Impact

- The preview pane shows the wrong note's content. A user reading a fragment before copying or
  referencing it can act on another snippet's text.
- The corruption is silent and sticky: nothing re-renders to correct it until `body`, `path`,
  `view`, `plugin` or `language` changes again for some other reason.
- The same effect also re-runs whenever `body` changes after an autosave
  (`body={dirty ? draft : body}`), so an in-flight save can be enough to trigger the race without
  the user switching fragments at all.

## Suggested fix

Track the current render in the effect and abandon it on cleanup, e.g. capture `path`/`body` and
verify them (or a monotonic token) after the promise resolves before allowing the write — or
re-render into a detached element and swap it in only if still current. `MarkdownRenderer.render`
accepts a component, which can also be used as the cancellation boundary:

```tsx
let cancelled = false;
void MarkdownRenderer.render(plugin.app, body, element, path, view).then(() => {
  if (cancelled) element.empty();
});
return () => { cancelled = true; };
```

## Notes

- No existing issue covers `Preview` or `MarkdownRenderer` (deduped against `br search` for
  `preview`, `MarkdownRenderer`, `render`, `race`, `stale render`, `markdown`).
- `GlobalSearch` has an equivalent un-awaited write pattern in
  `MarkdownRenderer`? No — it is DOM-only and synchronous, so it is not affected.
close_reason: the markdown preview now renders into a detached staging node and swaps it into the live element only while the effect is still current, so a render that resolves after the user switched fragments can no longer overwrite the newer preview; regression test tests/preview-race.test.tsx resolves the stale Alpha render last and asserts Beta stays visible

title: The auto-select effect yanks the selection to another fragment when an edit removes the open snippet from the active view, so later keystrokes are saved into the WRONG note (un-star while editing)
description:
## Summary

The auto-select effect in `useController` (`src/app.tsx`) keeps the selection inside the current
`filtered` list, but it applies that rule with **no exception for the fragment the user is actively
editing**. Any action that removes the *currently edited* fragment from `filtered` — un-starring it
while the Starred scope is active, for example — makes the guard immediately re-point the selection
at a **different fragment**. `useDraft` then loads that other fragment, and every keystroke the user
types afterwards is persisted **into the wrong note on disk**.

The user sees no error and no notice. The title input and the editor content both change to the
other snippet, but the user is mid-sentence in the fragment they believe they are editing, so the
remaining text is written to a different file.

## Root cause

```ts
// src/app.tsx — useController
useEffect(() => {
  if (selected && filtered.some((item) => item.path === selected)) return;
  setSelected(filtered[0]?.path ?? null);
}, [selected, entries, filtered]);
```

The guard treats "not present in `filtered`" as "invalid selection", which is correct for a
collection/tag/Recent scope change, but wrong for a fragment the user has open and is typing into.
`filtered` is a *view* predicate, not a validity check, and the two are conflated.

`filtered` is recomputed from `searchIndex`, which is rebuilt from `entries` on every library
revision, so the effect re-runs after **any** `updateProperties` — including one the user just
performed on the fragment they are editing:

```ts
const toggleStar = async (): Promise<void> => {
  if (!selectedItem) return;
  await library.updateProperties(selectedItem.path, { starred: !selectedItem.starred });
  // -> refresh() -> emit() -> new entries -> new filtered -> the guard above fires
};
```

`updateProperties` -> `refresh` -> `emit` re-derives the list, the just-unstarred fragment no longer
matches `scope = { kind: "starred" }`, the guard moves the selection to `filtered[0]`, and `useDraft`
tears down and loads the new path:

```ts
// src/app.tsx — useDraft, selection-change cleanup
useEffect(() => () => {
  const writing = pendingDraft.current;
  if (writing?.path === selected)
    void library.saveBody(writing.path, writing.text, savedBody.current).catch(errorNotice);
}, [selected, library]);
```

The already-typed text is flushed correctly. Everything typed **after** the jump goes to the new
fragment.

## Trigger

No search box and no unusual gesture is required:

1. Open the **Starred** scope.
2. Select a starred fragment and type into it (draft is unsaved or recently autosaved).
3. Click the **Star** button to un-star that same fragment — an ordinary single click.

The same class of trigger applies to any self-edit that drops the fragment out of the active view:
removing the tag that the active tag scope is filtering on, or editing away the term that the
active list-search query matched (the list search runs with `includeBody: true`, so editing a body
so it no longer contains the query term drops the fragment out of `filtered` the moment the autosave
re-indexes it).

## Impact

- **Silent cross-fragment data corruption.** Text the user intended for one note is written into a
  different note's Markdown file, and saved there.
- The UI gives no signal at all: no notice, no error, and the footer flips to "Saved" because the
  autosave genuinely succeeds — into the wrong file.
- The damage is one-directional and hard to notice. The original fragment keeps the text typed
  *before* the jump; the new fragment gains the text typed *after* it. The user who was "editing"
  the wrong note for the rest of the session sees a coherent-looking editor throughout.
- It compounds with the 700 ms autosave: the switch can happen on any revision bump, and the user is
  never told the document they are typing into changed.

## Reproduction (deterministic)

Real `AppShell` + real `FragmentLibrary` + real `searchFragments`, mounted in jsdom with React 19
against an in-memory vault holding two starred fragments, `Fragments/Alpha.md` and
`Fragments/Beta.md`. Only the vault and the Obsidian API are doubles; the components, hooks and
search code under test are the repository's own, bundled from `src/`.

Sequence: Starred scope -> Alpha selected -> type into the editor -> click Star (un-star) -> keep
typing.

Bug run:

```
=== 2. Starred scope active ===
title input : Alpha
rows        : 2

=== 3. user types an unsaved draft into the editor ===
editor after : "Alpha body text.\n PLUS-MY-DRAFT"
footer       : 31 chars · 4 wordsUnsaved changesSave changes

=== 4. user clicks Star (unstar) mid-edit ===
clicking     : Unstar fragment

=== 5. AFTER unstar — where did the editor go? ===
title input  : Beta   <-- which fragment is loaded
editor now   : "Beta body text.\n"
footer       : 16 chars · 3 wordsLast edited 1045d agoSaved
Alpha starred: false
notices      : []

=== 6. user keeps typing, believing they are still in Alpha ===
on disk Alpha.md:
  "...\n\nAlpha body text.\n PLUS-MY-DRAFT"
on disk Beta.md:
  "...\n\nBeta body text.\n SECOND-HALF-INTENDED-FOR-ALPHA"
```

`SECOND-HALF-INTENDED-FOR-ALPHA` was typed while the user believed they were in Alpha, and it is
now a permanent part of `Beta.md`. The notice list is empty, so nothing warned the user.

Control — the identical run with the Star click removed:

```
=== 4. CONTROL: no unstar click ===

=== 5. AFTER unstar — where did the editor go? ===
title input  : Alpha
editor now   : "Alpha body text.\n PLUS-MY-DRAFT"
footer       : 31 chars · 4 wordsUnsaved changesSave changes
Alpha starred: true

=== 6. user keeps typing ===
on disk Alpha.md:
  "...\n\nAlpha body text.\n PLUS-MY-DRAFT SECOND-HALF-INTENDED-FOR-ALPHA"
on disk Beta.md:
  "...\n\nBeta body text.\n"

CONTROL: selection stayed on Alpha and typing stayed in Alpha
  text intended for Alpha landed in Beta : false
```

Same vault, same typing, same scopes; the only difference is the single Star click. That isolates the
cause to the guard effect reacting to the un-star, not to the autosave, the search index, or the
selection cleanup.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** the fragment the user is editing keeps the editor, whatever happens to the
  surrounding view. Un-starring a snippet should update the list and the counts, and nothing else.
  If a filter does legitimately have to move the selection, it should not do so as a side effect of
  the user acting on the open snippet, and never while there are unsaved keystrokes in flight.
- **Actual:** un-starring silently re-points the selection to another fragment, and the user's
  subsequent typing is committed to that fragment's file.

## Suggested fix

Distinguish "the filter changed" from "the open fragment is no longer a match", and never move the
selection out from under an active draft. The guard needs to know whether the current selection was
made deliberately and whether the user is editing:

```ts
const editingPath = useRef<string | null>(null);   // set by edit(), cleared on flush
useEffect(() => {
  if (selected && filtered.some((item) => item.path === selected)) return;
  if (selected && editingPath.current === selected) return;   // keep editing the open note
  setSelected(filtered[0]?.path ?? null);
}, [selected, entries, filtered]);
```

A narrower fix that still removes the data-loss path is to make the move conditional on the open
fragment being clean, so the worst case is a selection change the user can see rather than a
diversion of their typing:

```ts
if (selected && dirty) return;
```

Ideally the editor would also be visually marked when the open fragment falls outside the active
view, so the situation is never silent.

## Relationship to existing issues

- `fragments-palette-pick-overridden-by-active-scope-gp9` involves the same effect, but a different
  trigger and a different fix: there a *palette* pick lands outside the active scope because
  `choosePalette` routes through `choose` instead of `chooseGlobal`, and the proposed fix is to clear
  the scope. **That fix would not help here**, because this trigger involves no pick at all — the
  user un-stars the fragment they are already editing, and clearing the scope still leaves the
  fragment outside `filtered`.
- `fragments-nzo` covers the same effect when it sets the selection to `null` (an empty search
  result): there the buffer ends up permanently blank and unsaveable, and the fix is in `useDraft`'s
  `!selected` branch. Here `filtered` is non-empty, a **different, valid** fragment is selected, the
  buffer looks perfectly healthy, and the failure is that later keystrokes are written to the wrong
  file. Different code path, different symptom, different severity.
- `fragments-w3w` also concerns `useDraft` and the same effect's inputs, but it is the load effect's
  stale `dirty` closure reverting a buffer. No selection move and no wrong-file write there.
- `fragments-tti` and `fragments-jyi` are draft-flush losses; here the draft *is* flushed correctly
  and the loss is the text typed after the selection moved.
close_reason: the auto-select effect now distinguishes a filter change from an entries update: it keeps the editor on a fragment that still exists when the user acts on it (un-star, tag, body edit) and only moves the selection when the filter changes or the fragment vanishes; regression test tests/auto-select-edit.test.tsx covers un-star mid-edit

title: rename() sanitises the filename but stores the raw title, and the collision guard then refuses titles that are not actually taken
description:
## Summary

`FragmentLibrary.rename` sanitises the **filename** but stores the **unsanitised title** in
frontmatter. Because the collision guard then tests the *sanitised* path against existing vault
files, renaming to a title that no fragment actually owns is refused with a message that is factually
wrong, and the rename that *is* accepted permanently splits a fragment's title from its filename.

## Affected code

`src/library.ts` — `FragmentLibrary.rename()`

```ts
async rename(path: string, title: string): Promise<string> {
  const file = this.file(path);
  const safe = title.trim().replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, "-");   // sanitised, used for the PATH
  if (!safe) throw new Error("Enter a title.");
  const next = `${file.parent?.path}/${safe}.md`;
  if (next !== path && this.app.vault.getAbstractFileByPath(next))
    throw new Error("A fragment with that title already exists.");   // guards on the SANITISED path
  await run(() => this.app.fileManager.renameFile(file, next));
  await run(() =>
    this.app.fileManager.processFrontMatter(file, (matter) => {
      const frontmatter = matter as { title?: string };
      frontmatter.title = title.trim();          // RAW title persisted, not `safe`
    }),
  );
  ...
}
```

Two consequences fall out of the `safe` / `title.trim()` split:

1. **`next` is derived from `safe`, so distinct titles collide.** `a/b`, `a:b`, `a?b` and `a|b` all
   sanitise to `a-b`. Whichever of those titles is used second is refused.
2. **The frontmatter keeps the raw title**, so after a successful rename the file is named
   `Q3-Q4 plan.md` while its frontmatter (and therefore the whole UI title) is `Q3/Q4 plan`.

`FragmentLibrary.fragmentFrom` then reads `matter.title ?? file.basename`, so the list, the search
index and `searchText` all key off the raw title while the file on disk is named after the
sanitised one. Nothing ever reconciles the two.

## Reproduction (deterministic)

Vault:

- `Fragments/a-b.md` with `title: a-b`
- `Fragments/keep.md` with `title: keep`

Drive the real `FragmentLibrary` (no React involved):

```ts
const library = new FragmentLibrary(app, { folder: "Fragments" });
await library.load();
await library.rename("Fragments/keep.md", "a/b");
```

Observed:

```
titles in library: ["a-b","keep"]
rename keep -> 'a/b': REFUSED -> A fragment with that title already exists.
```

No fragment is titled `a/b` — the blocking file is titled `a-b`. The guard fired on the sanitised
path, so the error message describes a collision that does not exist.

A title that needs no sanitising then splits title from filename:

```
rename keep -> 'Q3/Q4 plan' -> Fragments/Q3-Q4 plan.md
frontmatter on disk: "\ntitle: \"Q3/Q4 plan\"\ntags: []\nstarred: false\nlanguage: \"plaintext\"\n"
filename: Fragments/Q3-Q4 plan.md
indexed title: Q3/Q4 plan
title === basename? false
```

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** the title is the fragment's identity. A rename to a title that no fragment holds
  succeeds, and the title the user typed is what is stored and shown.
- **Actual:** the filename is a lossy projection of the title used as the *primary* key for
  collision detection, so (a) legitimate renames are refused with a misleading error, and (b) a
  successful rename leaves `title` and the file's basename permanently different.

## Impact

- Renaming to any title containing `/ \ : ? * " < > |` is refused whenever a fragment's title is the
  same string with those characters replaced by `-`. Date-style names hit this constantly
  (`2024/01/02` vs `2024-01-02`, `Q3/Q4` vs `Q3-Q4`).
- Once accepted, the fragment is permanently mis-filed relative to its own title, so the title the
  user sees never matches the file in Obsidian's file explorer, and the "rename" cannot be replayed
  to recover the original filename.
- The error text actively misleads: it claims a title conflict for a title that is free.

## Evidence notes

Observed with the real `FragmentLibrary` and real `rename()` implementation, driven by a mock vault
that implements the documented Obsidian contracts (`getAbstractFileByPath`, `renameFile`,
`processFrontMatter`). The finding does **not** depend on any assumption about frontmatter parsing
or on `Effect` scheduling: it follows directly from the `safe` vs `title.trim()` split, and the
refusal path never reaches `processFrontMatter` at all.

A separate, genuinely non-existent race in `create()` was tested and **falsified** in the same
harness: two concurrent `create()` calls are serialised because `Effect.tryPromise` invokes the
`vault.create` thunk synchronously, so the second call observes the first call's path and picks
`Untitled fragment 2.md`.
close_reason: rename() now refuses only titles another fragment actually holds, disambiguates the filename when a different title already owns the sanitised path (a/b vs a-b -> 'a-b 2.md'), and stores the requested title in frontmatter. Regression test tests/rename-title.test.tsx red-verified against the old path-based guard; full check green (11 files / 18 tests).

title: createCollection() flattens '/' to '-', so the New collection dialog and create()/move() create two different folders for the same name
description:
## Summary

`FragmentLibrary.createCollection` sanitises `/` to `-`, so a collection name containing a slash is
silently created as a **flat** folder. Every other collection-producing path in the plugin
(`create(collection)`, `move(path, collection)`, `ensureFolder`) treats the same string as a **nested**
path. Typing `work/reports` into the "New collection" dialog therefore creates `Fragments/work-reports`,
while creating or moving a fragment into `work/reports` creates `Fragments/work/reports`. Both end up
listed as collections, so the user's library is left with two different folders for the name they
typed, and neither one contains the fragments in the other.

## Root cause

```ts
// src/library.ts
async createCollection(name: string): Promise<void> {
  const safe = name.trim().replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, "-");   // <-- "/" becomes "-"
  if (!safe) throw new Error("Enter a collection name.");
  await this.ensureFolder(`${this.folder()}/${safe}`);     // one flat folder
  this.emit();
}
```

The other paths split the same input into real folder levels:

```ts
async create(collection = ""): Promise<string> {
  const folder = collection ? `${this.folder()}/${collection}` : this.folder();
  await this.ensureFolder(folder);          // ensureFolder walks parts and creates each level
  ...
}

async move(path: string, collection: string): Promise<string> {
  const folder = collection ? `${this.folder()}/${collection}` : this.folder();
  await this.ensureFolder(folder);
  ...
}
```

`createCollection` is the only producer of a collection path that collapses the separator, so the two
spellings of the same user input both become reachable. The dialog reports success either way — the
input's placeholder is just `Collection name`, with no indication that nesting is or is not happening.

## Reproduction

The real `src/library.ts` bundled with esbuild (`obsidian` aliased to a stub of `getFrontMatterInfo` /
`normalizePath` / `TFile` / `TFolder` plus an in-memory vault with a real parent chain). No React, no
timing.

```js
await library.load();
await library.createCollection("work/reports");   // "New collection" dialog
await library.create("work/reports");             // "New snippet" while that collection is selected
await library.move(created, "work/reports");      // Collection <select> in the properties row
```

Output:

```
after createCollection('work/reports') -> folders: [ 'Fragments', 'Fragments/work-reports' ]
   collections()                        : [ 'work-reports' ]
create('work/reports')                  : Fragments/work/reports/Untitled fragment.md
collections() now                       : [ 'work', 'work-reports' ]
all folders on disk                     : [
  'Fragments',
  'Fragments/work-reports',
  'Fragments/work',
  'Fragments/work/reports'
]
=> two spellings of 'work/reports' exist: true
```

Note `collections()` reports `['work', 'work-reports']`: the nested form appears as the two levels
`work` and `work/reports` (the intermediate folder is listed too, by design — `collections()` pushes
every folder it visits), while the dialog's form is a single unrelated row `work-reports`.

## Impact

- **Silent wrong destination.** The dialog closes and emits as if the collection were created, but a
  different folder path than intended exists on disk. The user has to inspect the vault to discover it.
- **The two spellings fragment the user's library.** Fragments the user believes are in one collection
  are split across two, so the sidebar's per-collection counts and the collection scope filter each
  report a fraction of the truth, and the two rows look like two different collections.
- **The collection the user just "created" may stay empty.** After `createCollection("work/reports")`,
  anything the user moves to `work/reports` lands in `Fragments/work/reports/...`, i.e. in a different
  folder than the one just created — so the dialog's collection is never used.
- Reachable from ordinary use: any user who types a slash in the dialog, and any vault that already has
  a nested collection, will have one of the two spellings and be offered the other.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** one collection path for one input string. Either the dialog nests like `create`/`move`
  do, or those two paths sanitise the same way.
- **Actual:** the same input yields two distinct folders, both listed as collections.

## Where to fix

`src/library.ts`, `createCollection`. It should agree with `create`/`move` — either create one level per
`/`-separated segment (sanitising each segment, not the separator) so `work/reports` produces
`Fragments/work/reports`, or reject `/` with a clear error. A regression test asserting
`createCollection(x)` and `create(x)` resolve to the same folder would pin the two paths together.

## Related but distinct

- `fragments-pdm` (folder-level events not re-indexing descendants) and `fragments-42n` (the Fragments
  *root* folder setting being matched case-sensitively) are about the root folder and index freshness.
  This is about a single collection path being spelled two different ways by two different functions in
  the same file.
- No existing issue covers `createCollection` at all.
close_reason: createCollection() now splits a slash-separated name into segments, sanitises each segment, and lets ensureFolder nest them, so the New collection dialog produces the same folder as create()/move(). Regression test tests/collection-path.test.tsx asserts both paths resolve to Fragments/work/reports and no flat work-reports folder is created; red-verified against the old flattening code; full check green (12 files / 19 tests).

title: useScratchpad latches a one-way conflicted flag, so one scratchpad write conflict permanently disables saving for the session
description:
## Summary

In `src/app.tsx`, `useScratchpad` marks a session `conflicted = true` the first time
any save rejects, and **nothing ever sets it back to `false`**. A single scratchpad
write conflict therefore disables scratchpad persistence for the entire remaining
lifetime of the plugin session, with no recovery path and (after the first Notice)
no further feedback at all.

## Root cause

`ScratchpadSession.conflicted` is a one-way latch:

- `src/app.tsx:823` — declared `conflicted: boolean`
- `src/app.tsx:865` — initialised to `false`, only ever inside the path-change effect
- `src/app.tsx:849` — set to `true` in the `flush` rejection handler

A repository-wide scan of every read/write of `conflicted` shows there is **no reset
site at all** (0 assignments of `conflicted = false` outside the constructor):

```
app.tsx:823  conflicted: boolean;
app.tsx:837  if (!current.ready || current.conflicted) return;          // flush guard
app.tsx:841  if (current.conflicted || next === current.saved) return;   // queued write guard
app.tsx:849  current.conflicted = true;                                  // latch set
app.tsx:865  conflicted: false,                                          // constructor only
app.tsx:899  if (current.conflicted) return;                             // edit guard
```

## Impact

The guards at `app.tsx:837`, `app.tsx:841` and `app.tsx:899` mean that once the latch
is set:

1. `flush` returns immediately, so the 500 ms debounce timer, the `onBlur` save and the
   Ctrl/Cmd+S path in `Scratchpad` all become no-ops.
2. `editScratchpad` returns **after** `setText(value)` but **before** `setStatus("dirty")`
   and before scheduling the new timer, so the textarea keeps accepting keystrokes and
   echoing them back, `current.text` advances, but nothing is ever written and the
   status is frozen on `"error"` ("Could not save").
3. The user is told once, via a Notice, and then gets a fully working-looking editor
   that silently discards everything they type. The only escape is closing and
   reopening the Fragments view, which remounts the effect and rebuilds the session.

The scratchpad is explicitly designed to be a *shared* file — it lives at
`Fragments/_fragments-scratchpad.md` in the vault and is documented as such — so an
external write is an expected, ordinary event, not a rare edge case. A second Obsidian
window on the same vault, Obsidian Sync, or the user editing that note directly all
trigger it. The condition is fully recoverable; only the UI refuses to recover.

## Evidence that the underlying data is not actually lost

`FragmentLibrary.saveScratchpad` has no memory of a past conflict. Re-reading the file
and retrying with the fresh baseline writes successfully:

```js
// after a conflict, with the file still present
await library.saveScratchpad(sp, "v2", "hello3");
// resolves and persists "v2"
```

So the loss is caused purely by the hook's latch, not by the library.

## Reproduction

1. Open Fragments, show the scratchpad, and give it content so a file exists at
   `Fragments/_fragments-scratchpad.md`.
2. Edit that note outside Fragments (another window, or sync) so its on-disk contents no
   longer match the session's `saved` baseline.
3. Type in the scratchpad. The 500 ms debounce fires, `saveScratchpad` throws
   "The scratchpad changed outside Fragments.", `conflicted` is latched, and the status
   switches to "Could not save".
4. Stop editing externally — the vault is fully consistent again.
5. Keep typing. Every keystroke updates the visible text; nothing is ever written; the
   status never changes again. Saving via blur or Ctrl/Cmd+S does nothing.

## Suggested fix

Give the session a way back. Either re-read the file and reset `current.saved` /
`current.conflicted` when the user edits after a conflict, or surface a "Reopen
scratchpad" / retry affordance that re-arms the session instead of leaving the editor
permanently inert.

## Related

Distinct from `fragments-tmf` (that report is about `run()`/Effect mangling error
messages; this latch is pure control flow in the hook and survives that fix) and from
`fragments-rt7` (frontmatter tag parsing).
close_reason: useScratchpad no longer latches conflicted; a rejected write re-reads the scratchpad as the new baseline and the next edit, blur or save retries instead of disabling the session

title: Clearing the Language field silently rewrites the fragment's frontmatter language to plaintext
description:
## Summary

Clearing the Language field and blurring it silently rewrites the fragment's
`language` frontmatter to `plaintext`, destroying the language the user had set (e.g.
`python` -> `plaintext`). The revert-on-invalid guard written into `LanguageInput` is
dead code for empty input, so the one action that should be a no-op is the one action
that mutates the note.

## Root cause

`src/languages.ts` treats an empty query as a valid selection instead of "no match":

```ts
export function findLanguage(value: string): LanguageChoice | undefined {
  const search = value.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (!search) return languageChoices[0];   // <-- "" resolves to the plaintext choice
  return languageChoices.find((choice) => choice.id === search || ...);
}
```

`languageChoices[0]` is the hardcoded `{ id: "plaintext", label: "Plain text" }` entry,
so `findLanguage("")` and `findLanguage("   ")` both return that choice rather than
`undefined`.

`LanguageInput` in `src/app.tsx` relies on `undefined` to mean "revert":

```tsx
const commit = useCallback((value: string) => {
    const choice = findLanguage(value);
    if (!choice) {                       // <-- unreachable for "" and whitespace
      setText(languageLabel(item.language));
      return;
    }
    setText(choice.label);
    if (choice.id !== item.language)
      void library.updateProperties(item.path, { language: choice.id }).catch(errorNotice);
}, [item.language, item.path, library]);
```

The input's `onBlur` calls `commit(text)`, so select-all + Delete + click-away resolves
to `choice.id === "plaintext"`, differs from the stored language, and writes it to the
file.

## Impact

A silent, unrequested write to the user's note, triggered by an ordinary "clear the
field" gesture. Because the language drives syntax highlighting in both Edit and Preview,
the fragment also visibly loses its highlighting. The revert branch shows the author
intended empty input to be rejected, so this contradicts the code's own contract.

## Steps to Reproduce

Observed with the real `languages.ts` and `FragmentLibrary` against an in-memory vault
stub.

1. Seed `Fragments/snippet.md` with `language: python` in its frontmatter.
2. Load the library.
3. In the UI, select all text in the Language field, press Delete, then click elsewhere
   to blur it. (Equivalent to calling `LanguageInput`'s `commit("")`.)

Observed `findLanguage` behaviour:

```
  findLanguage("")                   -> plaintext / Plain text
  findLanguage("   ")                -> plaintext / Plain text
  findLanguage("nonsense-language")  -> undefined
  findLanguage("") is undefined?     false
```

Observed file mutation for a fragment stored as `language: python`:

```
  frontmatter before: --- | title: "Snip" | tags: [] | starred: false | language: python | ---
  frontmatter after : --- | title: Snip  | tags:       | starred: false | language: plaintext
  languageLabel('python') = "Python"   <- the value commit() should have reverted to
```

In the UI this also shows up as a no-op-looking edit that still rewrites the file, so it
can fire while the user is only clearing the field to retype it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `findLanguage("")` and `findLanguage("   ")` return `undefined`, so empty input is
  rejected rather than resolved to a language.
- Clearing the Language field and blurring it leaves `language` frontmatter unchanged
  and restores the field to the fragment's current language label.
- Typing a real language name and blurring it still updates the frontmatter.
- The dead `if (!choice)` revert branch in `LanguageInput.commit` is now reachable, and
  a test covers the empty-string case.
close_reason: findLanguage now returns undefined for empty or whitespace-only input, so clearing the Language field reverts to the fragment's stored language instead of silently writing plaintext; regression test tests/language-input.test.tsx covers both the empty revert and a real language update

title: refresh()/indexBody() are unsequenced per path, so an out-of-order body read permanently overwrites the preview and the body search index
close_reason: indexBody() now stamps a per-path read sequence and drops any read that a newer read has superseded, so an out-of-order cachedRead can no longer overwrite the preview or body search index; remove() clears the sequence bookkeeping. Regression test tests/index-race.test.tsx forces the older refresh read to resolve last and asserts preview/searchText still hold EDITED-2 and body search finds it; red-verified with the guard removed; full check green (16 files / 23 tests).

title: Changing the Fragments folder setting with an unsaved draft open discards the draft and raises a spurious 'Fragment is no longer available.' notice
description:
## Summary

Changing the **Fragments folder** setting while the editor holds unsaved changes **silently discards the draft** and shows a misleading `Fragment is no longer available.` notice. Nothing is written to disk; the keystrokes are dropped and the buffer is replaced by the newly-selected fragment.

The draft *is* flushed — but the flush is rejected by the library's own folder guard, and the rejection is swallowed.

## Trigger

`FragmentsSettingTab.updateFolder` (`src/settings.ts`) calls `FragmentLibrary.changeFolder`, which mutates the folder **before** the library re-emits:

```ts
// src/library.ts — changeFolder()
async changeFolder(folder: string): Promise<void> {
  this.settings.folder = cleanFolder(folder) || "Fragments";   // <-- mutated synchronously, first
  await this.load();                                            // <-- emits, causing the React re-render
}
```

That `load()` → `emit()` drives `useController` to re-render. `selectedItem` becomes `undefined` (the old path is no longer in `entries`), so `useDraft` receives `selected === null` and its effect keyed on `selected` tears down.

The teardown flushes the pending draft:

```ts
// src/app.tsx — useDraft
useEffect(() => () => {
  const writing = pendingDraft.current;
  if (writing?.path === selected)
    void library.saveBody(writing.path, writing.text, savedBody.current).catch(errorNotice);
}, [selected, library]);
```

But `saveBody` resolves the file through a guard that is now scoped to the **new** folder:

```ts
// src/library.ts — file()
private file(path: string): TFile {
  const file = this.app.vault.getAbstractFileByPath(path);
  if (!(file instanceof TFile) || !this.contains(file.path))
    throw new Error("Fragment is no longer available.");
  return file;
}
```

`contains` prefixes the *current* `folder()`:

```ts
contains = (path: string): boolean => path.startsWith(`${this.folder()}/`) && ...
```

So the old path `Fragments/alpha.md` fails `startsWith("Notes/")`, `file()` throws, and `.catch(errorNotice)` turns the data loss into a `new Notice("Fragment is no longer available.")` that blames a problem that does not exist. The user is told the *fragment* is gone; the real cause is a settings change they deliberately made.

## Impact

- **Silent data loss**: the in-memory draft is destroyed. It was never written, and the plugin reports "Unsaved changes" -> "Saved" with the text simply gone.
- The notice is actively misleading: it names the fragment, not the folder change, so the user looks for a missing file that is still on disk.
- `docs/local-testing.md` check 6 instructs users to exercise exactly this flow (change the Fragments folder from the settings tab), so this is on the documented happy path, not an edge case.
- The same guard makes any in-flight write for a pre-change path fail, so the window is not limited to the 700 ms autosave debounce — an autosave already in flight is rejected the same way.

## Affected code

- `src/library.ts` — `changeFolder()` (mutates before re-index), `file()` / `contains()` (folder guard).
- `src/app.tsx` — `useDraft` selection-change/unmount cleanup (flushes to a path that is no longer in scope) and its `.catch(errorNotice)`.
- `src/settings.ts` — `updateFolder()` calls `changeFolder` while the view is mounted.

## Reproduction (deterministic)

Mounted the real `AppShell` in jsdom against an in-memory vault (two fragments, `Fragments/alpha.md` and `Notes/other.md`), typed into the editor, then invoked exactly what `updateFolder` does:

```
=== initial ===
rows: [ 'Alpha' ]
selected: Alpha
editor: "Body of Alpha\n"

=== after typing (unsaved) ===
editor: "MY UNSAVED WORK"
footer: 15 chars · 3 wordsUnsaved changesSave changes
alpha.md on disk: "\nBody of Alpha\n"

=== calling library.changeFolder('Notes') while the draft is open ===
rows now: [ 'Other' ]
editor after folder change: "Body of Other\n"
Notices shown to the user: ["Fragment is no longer available."]
alpha.md body on disk : "\nBody of Alpha\n"
Notes/other.md on disk: "\nBody of Other\n"

>>> 'MY UNSAVED WORK' still on disk anywhere? false
```

Instrumenting `library.saveBody` pins the mechanism exactly — the flush is attempted and rejected by the folder guard, not skipped:

```
trace:
   saveBody(path=Fragments/alpha.md) contains=false
     -> REJECTED: Fragment is no longer available.
notices: ["Fragment is no longer available."]
draft on disk anywhere: false
```

## Expected vs actual

**Expected** — changing the library folder while a draft is open should either (a) flush the draft to the file it belongs to *before* the folder setting moves, or (b) tell the user that unsaved changes in the old folder must be saved first. Either way the draft must reach disk and the notice must name the real cause.

**Actual** — the draft is dropped on the floor, the editor silently switches to a different fragment, and the user is told the fragment is "no longer available" when it is present and untouched.

## Distinct from related reports

- `fragments-tti` — `trash` is the one path-mutating action that does not flush the draft. Different trigger (toolbar action, not a settings change) and a different failure: there the flush is never attempted; here it is attempted and rejected by `contains()`.
- `fragments-nzo` — the selection is nulled by an empty search filter; the damage there is a permanently blank, unsaveable buffer. Here the damage is a discarded draft plus a false "no longer available" notice.
- `fragments-42n` — the folder setting is matched case-sensitively, so a case mismatch empties the library. Different defect and different symptom; this report is about in-flight writes to a pre-change path being rejected.
close_reason: changing the Fragments folder now flushes open drafts through the view shell before the library switches folders, so the draft reaches disk and the spurious 'Fragment is no longer available.' notice is gone; regression test tests/folder-change.test.tsx covers it

title: Tags are never case-normalised, so Work/work become two sidebar rows and the tag scope filter contradicts case-insensitive search
description:
## Summary

`FragmentLibrary.parseMetadata` strips a leading `#` from every frontmatter tag but never
normalises its case, so `tags: [Work]` and `tags: [work]` are stored and treated as two
different tags. `indexFragments` in `src/search.ts` *does* lowercase tags for text
matching, which makes this an internal inconsistency: **the same tag is matched
case-insensitively by search and case-sensitively by the tag filter**, so fragments a
query can find are unreachable by clicking the tag, and the sidebar renders duplicate
rows with fragmented counts.

## Root cause

Tags are normalised for one character only, never for case:

```ts
// src/library.ts:62  (inside parseMetadata)
tags: values.map((tag) => tag.replace(/^#/, "")).filter(Boolean),
```

That value flows straight into `Fragment.tags` and is used verbatim everywhere else:

```ts
// src/search.ts:34  — lowercased for MATCHING
tags: fragment.tags.map((tag) => tag.toLowerCase()),

// src/search.ts:47  — but the scope filter uses the RAW tag
case "tag":
  return item.tags.includes(scope.value ?? "");
```

```ts
// src/app.tsx:76  — sidebar counts are keyed by the RAW tag
for (const tag of item.tags) counts.set(tag, (counts.get(tag) ?? 0) + 1);
```

So `indexFragments` lowercases tags and then `matchesScope` ignores that lowercased
copy entirely and compares against the original casing.

## Impact

Given a vault with `tags: [Work]` on one note and `tags: [work]` on another:

- **The sidebar shows two rows** — `#Work` (1) and `#work` (1) — for what the user
  considers one tag, each undercounting.
- **The tag filter row in the list pane** (`app.tsx:775`) burns two of its five slots on
  the two spellings, crowding out other tags.
- **Clicking `#work` hides `#Work` notes.** The scope filter is case-sensitive, so no
  single tag click can ever show every note carrying that tag.
- **`countTags` truncates to the top 20** (`app.tsx:76-77`), so duplicated spellings
  displace genuinely distinct tags off the sidebar entirely.
- **Search and filtering disagree:** typing `work` into the list search matches
  case-insensitively through `searchText` and returns all three affected notes, while the
  tag click on the same string returns only the exactly-cased subset. Nested tags such
  as `area/work` compound this.

Obsidian treats tags case-insensitively, so this is reachable from ordinary vault content
rather than hand-crafted edge cases.

## Reproduction

Verified against the library with two notes whose frontmatter differs only in tag case
plus one nested-tag note:

```
Fragments/A.md  tags: [Work, js]
Fragments/B.md  tags: [work]
Fragments/F.md  tags: [area/work, "with space"]

query 'work'      -> A.md, B.md, F.md      (case-insensitive)
scope tag 'work'  -> B.md                  (case-sensitive)
scope tag 'Work'  -> A.md
distinct sidebar rows for "work" -> ["Work", "work"]
```

Notes A and B are returned by the query but there is no tag value that selects both.

## Suggested fix

Normalise tag case once, at parse time, so there is a single canonical form:

```ts
tags: values
  .map((tag) => tag.trim().replace(/^#/, "").toLowerCase())
  .filter(Boolean),
```

and render the original casing for display only if desired. That makes the scope filter,
the sidebar counts and `indexFragments` agree by construction. If tags are de-duplicated
case-insensitively instead, `matchesScope` must at minimum compare lowercased, and
`countTags` must key on the lowercased tag.

## Related

Distinct from `fragments-rt7`, which is about `parseMetadata` over-splitting a *scalar*
tag on whitespace (same function, different defect: different input, different symptom,
different fix). This report is about the *absent case normalisation* of array tags and
the consequent search-vs-scope mismatch.
close_reason: tags are now canonicalised to lowercase in parseMetadata and in the tag write path, so Work/work collapse into one sidebar row, the tag scope matches every casing, and search agrees with filtering; regression test tests/tag-case.test.tsx covers the sidebar row, the tag scope count and the lowercase write path

title: useKeyboard binds Ctrl+K/Ctrl+S on the whole Obsidian document, hijacking them for every pane in the window
close_reason: useKeyboard now ignores keydown events whose target is outside the Fragments view container, so ctrl+k/ctrl+s/escape no longer hijack the whole Obsidian window; regression test tests/keyboard-scope.test.tsx checks outside vs inside events

title: New collection dialog: Enter is a silent no-op because form?.requestSubmit() has no form ancestor
description:
## Summary

The "New collection" dialog handles Enter by calling
`event.currentTarget.form?.requestSubmit()`. Fragments renders **no `<form>` element
anywhere**, so `HTMLInputElement.form` is always `null`, the optional call
short-circuits, and pressing Enter in the dialog is a silent no-op. The user must
mouse the "Create collection" button.

The adjacent command palette *does* wire Enter correctly (`onKeyDown ... if (event.key === "Enter") choosePalette(paletteIndex)`),
so the two dialogs behave inconsistently. The dead `form?.requestSubmit()` line is
leftover intent that can never fire.

## Trigger

Open Fragments, click the "+" button next to the **Collections** heading in the
sidebar, type a collection name, and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. Nothing happens.

## Affected code

`src/app.tsx` — `Dialogs()`, the `dialog === "collection"` branch (line 1423):

```tsx
<input
  autoFocus
  value={newCollection}
  onChange={(event) => setNewCollection(event.target.value)}
  placeholder="Collection name"
  onKeyDown={(event) => {
    if (event.key === "Enter") event.currentTarget.form?.requestSubmit();   // <-- always a no-op
  }}
/>
<button
  className="fragments-primary"
  onClick={() => {
    void library
      .createCollection(newCollection)
      .then(() => { setNewCollection(""); setDialog(null); })
      .catch(errorNotice);
  }}
>
  Create collection
</button>
```

`requestSubmit` is invoked exclusively through `form?.`, and the collection-creation
logic lives in the sibling `<button>`'s `onClick`. No submit path is reachable from
the keyboard.

The `input`, the button and the `<div className="fragments-small-dialog">` wrapper
are all direct descendants of `<div className="fragments-overlay">`, which is itself
a plain `<div>`.

## Evidence

`HTMLInputElement.form` is, by spec, the nearest ancestor `form` element, or `null`
if there is none.

`src/app.tsx` is the only view source file that renders the dialogs
(`view.tsx` mounts `AppShell` into `contentEl`; `main.ts` only registers the view).
Searching the whole `src/` tree for any form element returns nothing but the
consuming line itself:

```
$ rg -n "<form|createEl\(\"form\"|\.form|requestSubmit" src/
src/app.tsx:1423:  if (event.key === "Enter") event.currentTarget.form?.requestSubmit();
```

There is no `<form>`, no `createEl("form")`, and no other `.form` / `requestSubmit`
reference in `src/`. The single match is the line that would need the ancestor to
exist. So `event.currentTarget.form === null` for this input, `?.` short-circuits,
and `requestSubmit()` is never called.

## Expected vs actual

- Expected: pressing Enter in the "New collection" dialog creates the collection and
  closes the dialog, matching the command palette in the same overlay and the
  "Fragments folder" setting text field, which both act on Enter.
- Actual: pressing Enter does nothing. The dialog stays open, no collection is
  created, and no notice or validation feedback is shown — the key press is
  silently absorbed.

## Impact

The dialog is the only way to create a collection from the UI, and the Enter
affordance is the expected one for a single text field. A user who types a name and
presses Enter sees no response at all, with nothing to indicate the value was not
submitted. It is a permanently unreachable code path that a reader would reasonably
assume is the submit route.

## Relationship to other reports

Distinct from `fragments-createcollection-flattens-nested-paths-4ht`, which is
about the collection *name* containing `/` being flattened to `-` and producing two
different folders. That report concerns `createCollection()` naming in
`src/library.ts`; this one is about the dialog's keyboard handling in
`src/app.tsx`. `br search requestSubmit` and `br search submit` return 0 issues.
close_reason: Enter in the New collection dialog now calls the same submitCollection handler as the Create collection button instead of the unreachable form?.requestSubmit(); the handler was extracted so both paths share validation, clearing and closing. Regression test tests/collection-dialog.test.tsx opens the dialog, types a name, presses Enter, and asserts the dialog closes and the collection exists; red-verified against the old form?.requestSubmit() line; full check green (13 files / 20 tests).

title: useDraft leaves a selected fragment blank and permanently unsaveable after the selection is nulled
description:
## Summary

In `src/app.tsx`, the `useDraft` hook clears `body`/`draft` when the selection becomes `null`, but leaves `dirty === true` and leaves `loadedPath.current` pointing at the last loaded path. The load guard then permanently refuses to reload that fragment, so the editor shows an **empty buffer for a fragment that has content**, the footer claims **"Unsaved changes"**, and every subsequent save fails the optimistic-concurrency check with a bogus "changed outside Fragments" error. The fragment becomes unsaveable until the user switches to another fragment and back.

## Root cause

`useDraft` (src/app.tsx) holds three pieces of state that must move together but do not:

- `dirty` — "the user has edits that are not on disk"
- `loadedPath.current` — "the path whose content is currently mirrored in `body`"
- `body` / `draft` — the buffer

The load effect resets the buffer but not the bookkeeping:

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (!selected) {
    setBody("");
    setDraft("");          // buffer wiped ...
    return undefined;       // ... but `dirty` stays true and loadedPath.current is left pointing at the old path
  }
  let active = true;
  void library.read(selected).then((text) => {
    if (active && (!dirty || loadedPath.current !== selected)) {   // guard now permanently false for that path
      loadedPath.current = selected;
      savedBody.current = text;
      setBody(text);
      setDraft(text);
      setDirty(false);
      pendingDraft.current = null;
    }
  }).catch(errorNotice);
  return () => { active = false; };
}, [selected, modified, library]);
```

`dirty` is also a stale closure value here (it is not a dependency of this effect), but that is secondary — the durable damage is `loadedPath.current === selected` combined with `dirty === true`.

The selection is nulled by this effect in `useController`:

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (selected && filtered.some((item) => item.path === selected)) return;
  setSelected(filtered[0]?.path ?? null);   // an empty `filtered` list nulls the selection
}, [selected, entries, filtered]);
```

Any search query with no matches empties `filtered`.

## Reproduction

1. Open Fragments, select a fragment (the list auto-selects the first one).
2. Type into the editor so there are unsaved edits. The footer shows "Unsaved changes".
3. Click the list search field and type a query that matches nothing, e.g. `zzzznomatch`.
   The list empties, `filtered` is `[]`, and `selected` becomes `null`.
   `useDraft`'s effect wipes `body`/`draft` to `""` but leaves `dirty === true`.
4. Clear the list search. `filtered` refills, `selected` returns to the same path.
5. **The editor is blank even though the file on disk still has its content, and the
   footer still reads "Unsaved changes" with an enabled "Save changes" button.**

Observed transcript from a jsdom harness that mounts the real `AppShell` against an
in-memory vault:

```
initial editor value: "ORIGINAL ALPHA BODY"
initial footer      : 19 chars · 3 wordsLast edited 0m agoSaved

[1] typed draft, footer: 41 chars · 7 wordsUnsaved changesSave changes
[2] no-match query, editor now: null
[3] editor after clearing filter: ""
[3] footer                     : "0 chars · 0 wordsUnsaved changesSave changes"
[3] file on disk still has     : "\n\nORIGINAL ALPHA BODY plus my unsaved draft"
```

Note `[3]`: the file on disk is intact, but the editor shows `""`.

## Impact

- **Data confusion:** the editor displays an empty fragment that in fact has content, so the
  user can believe a note was lost.
- **Unsaved work is rejected.** The next keystroke or Ctrl+S calls
  `library.saveBody(path, draft, body)` where `body` is the clobbered `""`. The
  optimistic-concurrency check in `FragmentLibrary.saveBody` compares `bodyOf(source)`
  against that `""`, fails, and raises the external-modification error — even though
  nothing outside Fragments touched the file. The fragment cannot be saved until the user
  selects a different fragment and comes back.
- The error is a false positive that erodes trust in the "don't clobber external edits"
  guarantee the README advertises.

## Where to fix

`useDraft` in `src/app.tsx`. When `selected` is cleared, the hook should invalidate its
bookkeeping rather than leaving a half-cleared state — e.g. also `setDirty(false)` and
reset `loadedPath.current` / `pendingDraft.current` (after the unmount-cleanup effect has
had a chance to flush the pending draft), or key the loaded path off a monotonically
increasing token so the `loadedPath.current !== selected` guard cannot be satisfied by a
stale path. A regression test that asserts "editor content is non-empty whenever a
fragment is selected" would pin this down.

## Environment

Found by executing the real `src/app.tsx` (bundled with esbuild, `obsidian` aliased to a
faithful stub) in jsdom + React 19 against an in-memory vault implementing
`getFrontMatterInfo` / `normalizePath` / `TFile` semantics.
close_reason: useDraft now resets dirty, loadedPath and pendingDraft together when the selection is cleared, so reselecting a fragment reloads its body instead of leaving a blank unsaveable buffer
