title: Folder-level vault events do not re-index descendant fragments, leaving permanently dead entries after a collection folder is renamed or deleted
description:
## Summary

`FragmentsPlugin.onload` only re-indexes **files**. Obsidian's `vault` emits a *single* event for a
renamed or deleted **folder**, with a `TFolder` as the subject — it does **not** emit per-descendant
file events. Because the handlers are guarded by `file instanceof TFile`, a folder-level change is
silently dropped, and every fragment underneath it stays in the index forever under its **old, dead
path**.

The result: the list pane still shows the snippets, but selecting one throws
`Fragment is no longer available.` and it never recovers — the index is only rebuilt by
`load()`, which runs on plugin load or when the Fragments-folder *setting* changes.

## Root cause

```ts
// src/main.ts:71-78
this.registerEvent(this.app.vault.on("delete", (file) => this.library.remove(file.path)));
this.registerEvent(
  this.app.vault.on("rename", (file, oldPath) => {
    this.library.remove(oldPath);
    if (file instanceof TFile) void this.library.refresh(file);   // <-- TFolder falls through
  }),
);
```

`remove(oldPath)` only drops the exact path of the event subject. For a folder rename,
`oldPath` is `Fragments/Work`, which was never a fragment, so it is a no-op — while the real
fragments live at `Fragments/Work/note.md`. Same for delete: the folder's own path is removed, its
descendants are not. `FragmentLibrary.contains` is the only place that knows about the
folder prefix, and no event handler consults it.

## Reproduction (deterministic)

1. Have `Fragments/Work/note.md` in the vault. Open Fragments — the list shows `note.md`.
2. In Obsidian's file explorer, rename the `Work` folder to `Projects`
   (or delete it outright).
3. Obsidian fires `vault.on("rename", <TFolder Projects>, "Fragments/Work")`.
   `file instanceof TFile` is false, so nothing is refreshed.

Observed with the real `FragmentLibrary` driven by a real `FragmentsPlugin.onload()`:

```
=== 1. initial index ===
entries: ["Fragments/Work/note.md"]
vault truth: ["Fragments/Work/note.md"]

=== 2. after renaming the folder Fragments/Work -> Fragments/Projects ===
vault truth: ["Fragments/Projects/note.md"]
entries : ["Fragments/Work/note.md"]
stale entries pointing at nothing: ["Fragments/Work/note.md"]

=== 3. can the UI still open what it lists? ===
  read("Fragments/Work/note.md") -> THROWS "Fragment is no longer available."

=== 4. does anything self-heal? ===
read via correct new path: "Body of the note.\n"
still listed under a dead path: true
```

Deleting the collection is worse — the fragments stay listed and readable-looking, but the files no
longer exist at all:

```
=== 5. same defect on folder delete ===
entries after folder delete: ["Fragments/Work/note.md"]
vault truth: []
deleted fragments still listed: 1
```

## Impact

- Renaming a collection folder in Obsidian makes every snippet inside it permanently unopenable
  from Fragments; the entry is still shown in the list and in search results, so the user clicks a
  row and gets an error instead of their note.
- Deleting a collection folder leaves permanently ghost rows in the list, search and tag counts
  (`countTags` still counts their tags), and the Starred/Recent quick-access counts.
- Recovery requires reloading the plugin or changing the Fragments-folder setting — neither is
  discoverable from the symptom.

## Suggested fix

Make the event handlers folder-aware: on `rename`/`delete`, if the subject is a `TFolder`, evict
every indexed path equal to or prefixed by the folder path (`Fragments/Work/`), and rebuild from
`vault.getMarkdownFiles()` for a rename. Note that `library.contains()` already encodes the folder
prefix, so the eviction predicate is simply
`p === oldPath || p.startsWith(oldPath + "/")`.

## Notes

- Distinct from `fragments-tti` (trash does not flush the draft) and from `fragments-tmf` (error
  message plumbing). Here the index itself is wrong; `library.read` rejects with a *correctly
  worded* `Fragment is no longer available.` because `file()` correctly refuses the stale path.
- Even when the message does surface, the underlying index is stale, so fixing only the message
  would not help.
close_reason: library.remove now evicts the whole subtree (folder events carry no per-descendant events) and folder renames trigger a full reload, so collection renames/deletes no longer leave dead entries

title: Preview keeps stale MarkdownRenderer results, so the pane shows another fragment's content
rename() is not atomic: a failure after fileManager.renameFile leaves a ghost entry for the old path and the renamed file unindexed and invisible
description:
## Summary

`FragmentLibrary.rename` performs two separate vault operations — `fileManager.renameFile` and then
`fileManager.processFrontMatter` — and updates its index in between. If the **second** step rejects,
the plugin has already moved the file on disk but never refreshes the new path. The result is a
library that is wrong in both directions at once:

- a **ghost entry** for the old path, whose file no longer exists (any later save fails with
  "Fragment is no longer available."), and
- the **real, renamed file is missing from the library** entirely, so it is invisible in the list,
  search, tags, and sidebar counts until the plugin is reloaded.

The `rename` promise rejects, so `app.tsx` skips `setSelected(await library.rename(...))` and the view
keeps `selected` pointing at the vanished old path.

## Root cause

```ts
// src/library.ts
async rename(path: string, title: string): Promise<string> {
  const file = this.file(path);
  const safe = title.trim().replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, "-");
  if (!safe) throw new Error("Enter a title.");
  const next = `${file.parent?.path}/${safe}.md`;
  if (next === this.scratchpadPath())
    throw new Error("That title is reserved for the scratchpad.");
  if (next !== path && this.app.vault.getAbstractFileByPath(next))
    throw new Error("A fragment with that title already exists.");
  await run(() => this.app.fileManager.renameFile(file, next));        // <-- step 1: already durable
  await run(() =>
    this.app.fileManager.processFrontMatter(file, (matter) => {      // <-- step 2: can reject
      const frontmatter = matter as { title?: string };
      frontmatter.title = title.trim();
    }),
  );
  this.remove(path);                                                   // <-- index drop
  await this.refresh(file);                                           // <-- never reached
  return file.path;
}
```

Three separate problems compound:

1. **No rollback.** Step 1 is already committed to disk when step 2 throws; nothing restores the old path.
2. **`remove(path)` runs after the failure point is reachable**, so a rejection leaves the old path
   *in* the map instead of out of it — the index is not merely stale, it is actively wrong.
3. **`refresh(file)` — the only thing that would index the new path — is skipped**, so the file the user
   just renamed is gone from the app.

Note the contrast with `move`, which has exactly the same two-step shape
(`renameFile` -> `remove` -> `refresh`) but only one vault write, so it cannot fail after the move.

`app.tsx` cannot recover either: `rename` is a single awaited call, and its catch only raises a Notice.

## Reproduction

The real `src/library.ts` bundled with esbuild (`obsidian` aliased to a stub of
`getFrontMatterInfo` / `normalizePath` / `TFile` / `TFolder` plus an in-memory vault with a real parent
chain). `processFrontMatter` is replaced so that **only step 2** rejects — this makes the failure
deterministic rather than timing-dependent; the structural defect and everything below are the real
code's behaviour.

```js
vault.seed("Fragments/Alpha.md", `---\ntitle: "Alpha"\ntags: ["work"]\nstarred: false\nlanguage: "python"\n---\n\nORIGINAL BODY`);
await library.load();
app.fileManager.processFrontMatter = async () => { throw new Error("could not parse frontmatter"); };
try { await library.rename("Fragments/Alpha.md", "Renamed"); } catch (error) { /* rejected */ }
```

Output:

```
before  : entries = [ 'Fragments/Alpha.md' ]
outcome : rename() REJECTED -> An unknown error occurred in Effect.tryPromise
on disk : [ 'Fragments/Renamed.md' ]
entries : [ 'Fragments/Alpha.md' ]
=> file on disk but absent from the library: true
=> refresh(path of the file on disk) recovers it:
   entries now: [ 'Fragments/Alpha.md', 'Fragments/Renamed.md' ]
```

The last two lines are the proof that the index — not the vault — is what is broken: a single
`refresh()` of the path that is actually on disk brings the real file back, and the ghost entry
(`Fragments/Alpha.md`) is still sitting there next to it.

(The rejection message is itself mangled to "An unknown error occurred in Effect.tryPromise" by
`run()`; that message-plumbing defect is tracked separately as `fragments-tmf` and is not what this
report is about.)

## Impact

- **The user's file becomes unreachable through the app.** A fragment they renamed disappears from the
  list, from search, and from every tag and collection count, with no way back except reloading the
  plugin or finding the file on disk. Nothing in the UI says the file moved.
- **A ghost row remains**, pointing at a path that no longer exists. Selecting it makes the editor
  useless and every save fail with "Fragment is no longer available."
- The failure is *reachable without any exotic condition*: `processFrontMatter` is the step that parses
  and re-serialises YAML, and the README explicitly supports notes "editable in Obsidian or any text
  editor", i.e. notes whose frontmatter was hand-written and may be malformed, or that use a shape the
  parser rejects. It is also the step that races with the concurrent vault events the plugin registers
  in `main.ts` (`vault.on("rename")` -> `library.refresh`), so a rename that coincides with an external
  or sync change can land in exactly this state.
- The user sees only a generic failure notice, so the natural conclusion is "the rename failed" — when in
  fact the rename **succeeded** and only the title write failed.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** either the whole rename is applied (file moved *and* frontmatter updated *and* index
  refreshed), or nothing changes and the old path still resolves.
- **Actual:** the file is moved, the index keeps the old path, the new path is unindexed, and the
  promise rejects.

## Where to fix

`src/library.ts`, `rename` (and the same shape in `move` for the shared pattern). Either make the
operation atomic by writing the frontmatter *before* `renameFile`, or compensate on failure: catch the
step-2 rejection, re-index the path that is actually on disk (`await this.refresh(file)` / `this.remove(path)`),
and rethrow with an accurate message. Index bookkeeping should happen only once the file is known to be
at `next`.

## Related but distinct

- `fragments-b99` covers the *filename sanitisation* half of `rename` (`safe` vs the raw title). This
  report is about the non-atomic two-step write and the index update that follows it; fixing the
  sanitisation does not fix a partial failure.
- `fragments-pdm` covers folder-level events failing to re-index descendants. This is a single-file
  index divergence created by `rename` itself, and it needs no folder rename to occur.
- `fragments-tmf` covers the mangled error message, not the partial state it reports.
close_reason: rename() now re-indexes the moved file as soon as the vault rename succeeds and reports a distinct error if the title write fails, so no ghost old-path entry and no invisible renamed file remain

title: Title rename on blur is async and overwrites the user's explicit fragment selection
description:
## Summary

`src/app.tsx` renames a fragment from the title input's `onBlur`, and the rename is
asynchronous. A normal click on a *different* row in the fragment list blurs the title
input first, so the click and the rename race. The rename's trailing
`setSelected(...)` lands after the click's `setSelected(...)` and wins, so clicking a
row while the title input holds uncommitted text opens the *renamed* fragment instead
of the one that was clicked.

## Root cause

`src/app.tsx`:

```tsx
const rename = async (value: string): Promise<void> => {
  if (!selectedItem || value.trim() === selectedItem.title) return;
  try {
    await save(false);
    setSelected(await library.rename(selectedItem.path, value));   // <-- async, unguarded
  } catch (error) {
    errorNotice(error as Error);
  }
};
```

and the toolbar input that triggers it:

```tsx
<input
  key={`${selectedItem.path}:${selectedItem.title}`}
  defaultValue={selectedItem.title}
  onBlur={(event) => void rename(event.target.value)}   // fires on mousedown of any click
  onKeyDown={(event) => { if (event.key === "Enter") event.currentTarget.blur(); }}
/>
```

`library.rename` awaits `fileManager.renameFile` and `processFrontMatter` before
resolving, so the window between the click's `choose(path)` and the rename's
`setSelected(newPath)` is always at least one I/O turn. The selection is not
re-validated, so the stale write clobbers the user's explicit choice.

## Impact

The user's click is silently discarded. This fires for any toolbar control that blurs
the input, not just list rows: Star, Copy, Preview/Edit, the scratchpad toggle and
Move to trash. With Move to trash the two operations interleave and the fragment is
renamed and *not* trashed, while the user gets a "Fragment is no longer available."
notice instead of the deletion they asked for.

## Reproduction

Verified by mounting the real `AppShell` in jsdom against an in-memory vault stub
(three fragments, no title edit in the control case):

1. Fragments `Alpha` and `Beta` exist; `Alpha` is selected.
2. Type `Alpha Renamed` into `.fragments-title-wrap input` (no Enter).
3. Click the `Beta` row — mousedown blurs the input, so `rename("Alpha Renamed")` starts.
4. Observed after settling: selected fragment is `Alpha Renamed`, not `Beta`.

Library trace for that run:

```
  >> rename("Fragments/Alpha.md", "Alpha Renamed")
  >> refresh(<obj>)
  << refresh ok
  << rename ok
after settle:            title input = "Alpha Renamed"
files: ["Fragments/Beta.md","Fragments/Alpha Renamed.md"]
```

Control case (step 2 omitted) lands on `Beta` as expected, confirming the pending
rename is the cause.

## Suggested fix

Make the rename selection-scoped: capture the path the rename was issued for and only
apply `setSelected` if the current selection still refers to the original fragment, e.g.

```tsx
const rename = async (value: string): Promise<void> => {
  const source = selectedItem?.path;
  if (!source || value.trim() === selectedItem?.title) return;
  try {
    await save(false);
    const next = await library.rename(source, value);
    setSelected((current) => (current === source ? next : current));
  } catch (error) { errorNotice(error as Error); }
};
```

`move` has the same shape and should get the same guard.

## Steps to Reproduce

Mount the real `AppShell` in jsdom against an in-memory vault stub (three fragments,
`Alpha` and `Beta` at the vault root), with the real `FragmentLibrary` and a stubbed
`obsidian` module.

1. Seed `Fragments/Alpha.md` (title `Alpha`) and `Fragments/Beta.md` (title `Beta`).
2. Mount `<AppShell />`; `Alpha` is auto-selected.
3. Type `Alpha Renamed` into `.fragments-title-wrap input`. Do **not** press Enter.
4. Click the `Beta` row (`.fragments-result` whose text contains `Beta`). Mousedown
   blurs the title input, which starts the rename; the click selects `Beta`.
5. Wait for the rename I/O to settle (~200 ms) and read
   `.fragments-title-wrap input`.

Expected: the selected fragment is `Beta`.
Actual: the selected fragment is `Alpha Renamed`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Renaming a fragment no longer changes the selection of a *different* fragment that the
  user selected after the blur but before the rename resolved.
- Clicking any fragment list row, and clicking the Star, Copy, Edit/Preview, scratchpad
  toggle and Move to trash controls, always leaves the selection on the clicked target.
- Move to trash while the title input holds uncommitted text trashes the fragment rather
  than failing with "Fragment is no longer available."
- A regression test covers: rename-then-click-row, and rename-then-click-trash, asserting
  the final selection and the resulting vault state.
close_reason: rename/move/trash are serialized through one mutation queue and selection is only retargeted when it still points at the fragment the mutation was issued for; relocated paths are resolved for trailing mutations

title: parseMetadata splits scalar frontmatter tags on whitespace, so 'tags: work notes' becomes two tags and the app's tag write path is lossy
description:
## Summary

`parseMetadata` in `src/library.ts` splits **scalar** frontmatter tags on `/[,\s]+/`, so a tag
containing a space is silently broken into two tags. The write path is not symmetric: `updateTags`
in `src/app.tsx` splits user input on **commas only**, so a single tag containing a space is
written intact and then comes back as two different tags.

Net effect: the tag set is not a round-trip. Writing one tag loses it.

## Root cause

```ts
// src/library.ts, parseMetadata
const tagValue = Option.getOrElse(decodeTags(raw?.tags), () => [] as string[]);
const values = Schema.is(Schema.String)(tagValue) ? tagValue.split(/[,\s]+/) : tagValue;
...
tags: values.map((tag) => tag.replace(/^#/, "")).filter(Boolean),
```

The read path treats whitespace as a separator. The write path does not:

```ts
// src/app.tsx, updateTags
tags: value
  .split(",")
  .map((tag) => tag.trim().replace(/^#/, ""))
  .filter(Boolean),
```

`updateTags("work notes")` therefore produces `["work notes"]`, which `updateProperties` writes to
frontmatter as-is. On the next read the scalar is re-split into `["work", "notes"]`.

Obsidian's `metadataCache` also collapses a single-element tag sequence to a plain scalar, so
`tags: ["work notes"]` written by Fragments is read back as the string `work notes` and hits the
splitting branch even when the file itself is untouched. The same branch fires for ordinary
hand-written frontmatter, which the README explicitly supports: *"The files remain editable in
Obsidian or any text editor."*

## Impact

- Silent data loss on write: a tag the user typed is replaced by two unrelated tags.
- The corruption is persistent and self-reinforcing — the sidebar tag list, the tag scope filter
  and the tag filter row all re-derive from the split value, so the UI presents the wrong tags as
  if they were what was entered.
- Any tag a user writes by hand with a space is fragmented on load, even if Fragments never wrote it.

## Reproduction

The real `src/library.ts` bundled with esbuild (`obsidian` aliased to a faithful stub of
`getFrontMatterInfo` / `normalizePath` / `TFile` plus an in-memory vault).

**Case A — hand-written frontmatter, no Fragments write involved:**

```
frontmatter `tags: work notes` -> ["work","notes"]   (expected one tag 'work notes')
```

**Case B — the app's own write path (round-trip):**

```
B) wrote tags ['work notes']; file frontmatter now: "title: \"N\"\ntags: [\"work notes\"]\nstarred: false\nlanguage: \"plaintext\""
B) read back -> ["work","notes"]   (expected ['work notes'])
B) lossless round-trip: false
```

The file on disk still holds exactly the value Fragments wrote; only the read path destroys it.

## Suggested fix

Make the read path agree with the write path — split scalar tags on commas only, and leave
whitespace intact:

```ts
const values = Schema.is(Schema.String)(tagValue) ? tagValue.split(",") : tagValue;
```

If splitting on whitespace is wanted for hand-edited files, the write path must apply the same rule
(and be documented as lossy); the current asymmetry is the defect either way. Normalising with
`tag.trim()` in both places would also make a stray `"a, b, ,c"` parse consistently.

A regression test asserting `updateTags(x)` -> `library.entries()[0].tags` is identity for inputs
containing spaces would pin this down.

## Note

Distinct from `fragments-tmf` (which is about `run()` swallowing error messages) and from the
`useDraft` issues (`fragments-nzo`, `fragments-tti`): this one is a parsing/round-trip defect in
`parseMetadata` and `updateTags` and has no dependency on draft state, the write queue, or error
plumbing.
close_reason: parseMetadata now splits scalar tags on commas only and trims each tag, matching the comma-joined write path, so 'work notes' round-trips as one tag; regression test tests/tag-roundtrip.test.tsx covers scalar read, write round-trip and comma splitting

title: Rejected rename leaves the title input showing a title the fragment does not have (uncontrolled field, key never changes)
description:
## Summary

The fragment title input in the editor toolbar is **uncontrolled** (`defaultValue`,
no `value` prop) and its React `key` is derived from `selectedItem.path` and
`selectedItem.title`. When `library.rename()` rejects a rename, the frontmatter title
is unchanged, so `selectedItem.title` is unchanged, so the `key` is unchanged, so
React never remounts the input and never rewrites the DOM value. The rejected text
stays in the header input while the fragment's real title, the list, the sidebar and
the search index all still hold the old one. The editor header keeps displaying a
title that was never applied, for as long as the user stays on that fragment.

## Trigger

1. Create a fragment titled `Beta` (it lands at `Fragments/Beta.md` with frontmatter
   `title: Beta`).
2. Select a different fragment, `Alpha`.
3. Click into the title input and type `Beta`.
4. Blur (click away or press Enter).

`library.rename` finds `Fragments/Beta.md` already taken and throws
`"A fragment with that title already exists."` A Notice is shown, the rename is
rejected — and the title input still reads `Beta`, while the fragment is `Alpha`.

## Affected code

`src/app.tsx` — `EditorToolbar()`:

```tsx
<input
  key={`${selectedItem.path}:${selectedItem.title}`}   // <-- only remount trigger
  aria-label="Fragment title"
  defaultValue={selectedItem.title}                    // <-- uncontrolled; no value prop
  onBlur={(event) => void rename(event.target.value)}
  onKeyDown={(event) => {
    if (event.key === "Enter") event.currentTarget.blur();
  }}
/>
```

and the handler, in `useController`, which swallows the failure without restoring
the field:

```tsx
const rename = async (value: string): Promise<void> => {
  if (!selectedItem || value.trim() === selectedItem.title) return;
  try {
    await save(false);
    setSelected(await library.rename(selectedItem.path, value));
  } catch (error) {
    errorNotice(error as Error);        // <-- no reset of the input; nothing re-renders it
  }
};
```

The rejection originates in `src/library.ts`, `FragmentLibrary.rename()`:

```ts
if (next !== path && this.app.vault.getAbstractFileByPath(next))
  throw new Error("A fragment with that title already exists.");
```

## Evidence

Two independent properties combine:

1. **The input is uncontrolled.** `defaultValue` with no `value` prop means React
   sets the DOM value only on mount. On re-render React deliberately does not touch
   the DOM value of an uncontrolled input, so the user's rejected text persists
   verbatim.
2. **The `key` cannot change on failure.** The key interpolates
   `selectedItem.title`, which is derived from the file's frontmatter
   (`fragmentFrom`: `matter.title ?? file.basename`). The throw happens *before*
   `fileManager.renameFile` and `processFrontMatter`, so the frontmatter is never
   written, `library.refresh()` never runs for the new title, and
   `selectedItem.title` is bit-identical before and after. Same key, same React
   element identity, no remount, no value reset.

The same happens for any rejection reason, not just the name collision — an empty
title (`"Enter a title."`), a title sanitising to the reserved scratchpad name
(`"That title is reserved for the scratchpad."`), or a vault error. In every case
`selectedItem.title` is unchanged and the field is never restored.

## Expected vs actual

- Expected: when a rename is rejected, the title input reverts to the fragment's
  actual title, so the header never shows a title the fragment does not have.
- Actual: the header continues to show the rejected text indefinitely. The user
  sees `Beta` in the editor header while the list row, the sidebar collection list
  and the on-disk frontmatter all still say `Alpha`. The only recovery is to switch
  fragments (changing `selectedItem.path`) or to complete a later *successful*
  rename, which changes the title and finally remounts the field.

## Impact

The editor header is the authoritative-looking display of the current fragment's
title, and it silently diverges from the stored title. A rename that was explicitly
rejected continues to look applied. This compounds with the already-reported
`-o57` race: because `onBlur` fires on the mousedown of *any* click (Star, Copy,
Preview/Edit, scratchpad toggle, Move to trash), a rejected rename triggered by an
incidental blur leaves the bogus title in place while the user proceeds to the next
action, so the desync survives the interaction that caused it.

## Relationship to other reports

- `fragments-rename-on-blur-races-and-overrides-list-selectio-o57` is about the
  *successful* rename path: its trailing `setSelected` clobbering the user's row
  click. It does not cover rejection.
- `fragments-b99` is a `src/library.ts` defect: the filename is sanitised while the
  raw title is persisted, so the collision guard rejects titles that are not
  actually taken. This report is about `src/app.tsx` never restoring the
  uncontrolled field when *any* rejection occurs, independent of whether the
  rejection is correct.
- `fragments-rename-non-atomic-partial-failure-w6w` is about `rename()` leaving a
  ghost index entry on a mid-flight failure; it does not concern the view's
  displayed title.
close_reason: useController.rename now reports whether the rename was applied, and the uncontrolled title input restores selectedItem.title whenever it was not (rejected or no-op) and the element is still mounted. Regression test tests/rename-reject.test.tsx renames Alpha to the taken title Beta and asserts the input snaps back, the notice fires, and both frontmatters stay unchanged; red-verified with the old void onBlur; full check green (14 files / 21 tests).

title: library run() helper swallows every vault error message, surfacing 'An unknown error occurred in Effect.tryPromise'
description:
## Summary

`src/library.ts` funnels every vault operation through a one-line helper:

```ts
const run = <A>(operation: () => Promise<A>): Promise<A> =>
  Effect.runPromise(Effect.tryPromise(operation));
```

`Effect.tryPromise` turns a rejected promise into a `Cause`, and `Effect.runPromise`
rejects with a `FiberFailure` wrapper rather than the original `Error`. The app displays
`error.message` in its notices, so **the user never sees the message the code actually
threw** — every such failure surfaces as the literal string:

> An unknown error occurred in Effect.tryPromise

This defeats the plugin's own conflict-detection UX, which exists specifically to tell
the user what to do next.

## Root cause

`run` is applied to the promises returned by `vault.process`, `vault.create`,
`vault.createFolder`, `vault.cachedRead`, `vault.read`, `fileManager.renameFile`,
`fileManager.processFrontMatter` and `fileManager.trashFile`. Every `throw new Error(...)`
that happens *inside* one of those callbacks is therefore converted to a `Cause` and lost.

Notably, the guard clauses that throw *outside* `run` are unaffected, which isolates the
root cause to `run` itself and makes the contrast easy to verify.

The callers all assume a normal `Error`:

```ts
// src/app.tsx
const errorNotice = (error: Error): void => {
  new Notice(error.message);
};
```

## Affected messages

These actionable messages exist in `src/library.ts` and are all destroyed by `run`:

| Site | Message the code intends to show |
| --- | --- |
| `saveBody` | "This note changed outside Fragments. Copy your draft, then reopen the note before saving." |
| `saveScratchpad` | "The scratchpad changed outside Fragments. Copy your text, then reopen Fragments before saving." |
| `saveScratchpad` | "The scratchpad file was removed outside Fragments." |

(the last one is thrown *outside* `run`, so it currently survives — see reproduction case 3)

Any real vault-level failure is equally opaque: adapter errors, permission failures,
"file already exists" from `create`, `normalizePath` rejections, etc.

## Impact

- The conflict-detection feature the README advertises ("avoids overwriting a note changed
  while a draft was open") is technically working but its message is useless: the user
  sees "An unknown error occurred in Effect.tryPromise" with no indication that their draft
  is at risk or that they should copy it somewhere safe.
- This actively masks data loss. The same harness shows a fragment becoming unsaveable
  (see the companion `useDraft` issue) — the user is told an opaque internal message
  instead of "copy your draft", so they are likely to force a fix by switching fragments,
  which discards the buffer.
- Any user attempting to self-diagnose a vault problem has nothing actionable to go on.

## Reproduction

Harness: the real `src/library.ts` bundled with esbuild, `obsidian` aliased to a
faithful stub of `getFrontMatterInfo` / `normalizePath` / `TFile` / an in-memory vault,
plus the repo's real `effect@3` dependency.

```
library.saveBody(path, 'x', 'stale-expected-body')
    intended : This note changed outside Fragments. Copy your draft, then reopen the note before saving.
    surfaced : An unknown error occurred in Effect.tryPromise
    => MESSAGE LOST

library.saveScratchpad(path, 'second', 'stale')
    intended : The scratchpad changed outside Fragments. Copy your text, then reopen Fragments before saving.
    surfaced : An unknown error occurred in Effect.tryPromise
    => MESSAGE LOST

library.saveScratchpad(path, 'text', 'non-empty')  // file removed
    intended : The scratchpad file was removed outside Fragments.
    surfaced : The scratchpad file was removed outside Fragments.
    => ok

library.trash(path) on a file the vault refuses to delete
    intended : permission denied
    surfaced : An unknown error occurred in Effect.tryPromise
    => MESSAGE LOST
```

Case 3 passes because that `throw` is in `saveScratchpad`'s own body rather than inside the
callback handed to `run` — direct confirmation that `run` is the defect. Cases 1, 2 and 4
are all throws raised inside a `run`-wrapped callback.

## Where to fix

`src/library.ts`. Either drop the `effect` dependency from this helper and just return the
promise, or unwrap the `Cause` before rethrowing — e.g.

```ts
import { Cause, Effect } from "effect";

const run = async <A>(operation: () => Promise<A>): Promise<A> => {
  const exit = await Effect.runPromiseExit(Effect.tryPromise(operation));
  if (exit._tag === "Success") return exit.value;
  const failure = Cause.failureOption(exit.cause);
  throw Cause.squash(exit.cause); // rethrows the original Error when there is one
};
```

Note that the rest of `library.ts` uses `effect` only for `Option` / `Schema` decoding in
`parseMetadata`, so removing the `run` helper is a one-line change and leaves the real
functional usage of the dependency in place.

A regression test asserting that `saveBody`'s conflict error message survives to
`error.message` would prevent this from silently returning.
close_reason: run() no longer wraps vault rejections in Effect.tryPromise; original Error messages now reach Notice

The stub-fidelity caveat is eliminated for this issue. The defect reproduces using only

title: VirtualList never resets scrollTop when the list shrinks, so filtering after scrolling renders zero rows while the header still reports matches
description:
## Summary `VirtualList` in `src/app.tsx` derives its rendered row window from a `scrollTop` **state value that is never reset when the item list shrinks**. Narrow the list search after scrolling down, and the computed window falls entirely outside the new, much shorter list, so **zero rows are rendered** while the list header still reports the correct fragment count. The list pane goes blank while claiming that matches exist. The component resets nothing on a list change: `scrollTop` is only ever written by the container's own `onScroll` handler. ## Root cause ```tsx // src/app.tsx — VirtualList const viewport = useRef(null); const [scrollTop, setScrollTop] = useState(0); ... const rowHeight = 88; const start = Math.max(0, Math.floor(scrollTop / rowHeight) - 4); const end = Math.min(items.length, Math.ceil((scrollTop + height) / rowHeight) + 4); return (
setScrollTop(event.currentTarget.scrollTop)} // <-- only writer >
{items.slice(start, end).map((item, index) => ( /* rows */ ))}
); ``` `start` is clamped to `0` but **not** to `items.length`. When `items.length` drops below `scrollTop / rowHeight - 4`, then `start > end` and `items.slice(start, end)` is `[]`, so the component renders no rows at all. There is no effect that clamps or resets `scrollTop` when `items` changes length. `scrollTop` is genuine component state, and the spacer div's height is driven by `items.length`, so the two diverge the moment the list is filtered. ## Trigger Any sequence of: scroll the list away from the top, **then** reduce the number of matching fragments — by typing in the list search, by picking a Starred/collection/tag scope, or by clicking a tag chip. Nothing exotic is required; the search box is right above the list. ## Impact - The list pane shows **no rows** while the summary line still reads e.g. "3 snippets", so the user is told there are matches they cannot see or select. - The selected fragment may also be scrolled out of the rendered window, so the editor and the list disagree about what is open. - Recovery depends entirely on the user scrolling the list manually (or on the browser clamping `scrollTop` when the scrollable area shrinks, which is not guaranteed to produce a `scroll` event). The application itself never corrects the stale offset. ## Reproduction (deterministic) Real `AppShell` + real `FragmentLibrary` in jsdom + React 19, against an in-memory vault with 63 fragments (`snip-00`..`snip-59` plus three containing the needle `zqmarker`). The scroll position is set and a real `scroll` event dispatched, i.e. exactly what a user scroll produces. `ResizeObserver` is a no-op, so the component keeps its initial `height = 600`. Bug run — scroll down, then filter: ``` === 1. full list === summary : "63 snippets" rows rendered : 11 spacer height : 5544px === 2. scroll far down the list === scrollTop set : 2000 rows rendered : 16 === 3. narrow the list search to 3 matches === summary : "3 snippets" rows rendered : 0 spacer height : 264px scrollTop now : 2000 (the app never resets it) BUG: header claims "3 snippets" but renders 0 rows -> true ``` The arithmetic is the whole story: `start = floor(2000/88) - 4 = 18`, `end = min(3, ...) = 3`, so `items.slice(18, 3)` is empty, even though `filtered.length === 3` and the spacer is now only 264px tall — the offset is already more than seven screens past the end of the content. Control — same filter, no prior scrolling: ``` === 2. CONTROL: filter without scrolling first === summary : "3 snippets" rows rendered : 3 ``` Identical data and identical query; only the stale `scrollTop` differs. That isolates the cause to the un-reset scroll offset rather than to the filtering, the search index, or the row count. ## Expected vs actual - **Expected:** when the list of items changes — particularly when it becomes much shorter — the rendered window is clamped to the new list, and any scroll offset past the end of the new content is corrected, so the rows that match the query are visible. - **Actual:** the window is computed from a stale offset, `start` overshoots `items.length`, and the component renders zero rows while still reporting the correct count. ## Suggested fix Clamp the window to the item list and reset the offset when the list changes. Minimal version: ```tsx const [scrollTop, setScrollTop] = useState(0); useEffect(() => { const node = viewport.current; if (!node) return; const max = Math.max(0, items.length * rowHeight - node.clientHeight); if (node.scrollTop > max) node.scrollTop = max; // reset on the real element setScrollTop(Math.min(scrollTop, max)); }, [items.length, height]); ``` and clamp the indices so an out-of-range offset can never produce an empty slice: ```tsx const start = Math.min(Math.max(0, Math.floor(scrollTop / rowHeight) - 4), items.length); const end = Math.max(start, Math.min(items.length, Math.ceil((scrollTop + height) / rowHeight) + 4)); ``` ## Notes and caveats - **Browser-dependence, stated honestly:** in a real browser, shrinking the spacer from 5544px to 264px may cause the engine to clamp `scrollTop` and fire a `scroll` event, which would self-correct the view. That is browser behaviour, not application behaviour, and it is not guaranteed to emit an event. What is demonstrated here and is independent of the browser is the application defect itself: **the component has no logic that clamps or resets its scroll offset when the item list shrinks**, and for any offset past the end of the new list it renders an empty window. The harness deliberately did not inject a corrective scroll event. - This is not the "no fragments found" empty state — that branch only renders when `filtered.length === 0`. Here `filtered.length` is 3 and the empty state is deliberately not shown, so the user gets a blank list with no explanation. - No existing issue covers the list virtualization: `br search` for `virtual`, `virtualized`, `scroll`, `scrollTop` and `spacer` each return 0 issues.
close_reason: VirtualList now clamps its rendered window against the current item count and resets a scrollTop past the end of the shrunken spacer, both in the render offset and in an items.length/height effect that writes the real element. Regression test tests/list-scroll.test.tsx scrolls a 33-fragment list, filters to 3 matches, and asserts 3 rows render with the summary and scrollTop reset; red-verified against the old unclamped window; full check green (15 files / 22 tests).

title: createCollection() has no scratchpad reservation guard: a collection named _fragments-scratchpad.md creates a FOLDER at the scratchpad path, permanently breaking the scratchpad
description:
## Summary

`FragmentLibrary.createCollection()` has **no reserved-name guard**, even though the two sibling
producers of a collection path — `rename()` and `move()` — both explicitly refuse to let anything
take the scratchpad's path. The result is that a single collection named `_fragments-scratchpad.md`
creates a **folder** at the exact path the scratchpad needs, and the scratchpad is then permanently
unusable: both its read and its write throw for the rest of the session.

There is no error at the moment of creation. The dialog closes, the sidebar gains a row, and the
user is never told that a documented feature has just been disabled.

## Trigger

1. Open Fragments and click the **+** next to the **Collections** heading in the sidebar.
2. Type `_fragments-scratchpad.md` (any string whose sanitised form equals the scratchpad's
   basename works; `_` and `.` are not in the sanitiser's replace set).
3. Click **Create collection**.

`createCollection` sanitises with `.replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, "-")`. The scratchpad basename
`_fragments-scratchpad.md` contains none of those characters, so it passes through **unchanged** and
`ensureFolder("Fragments/_fragments-scratchpad.md")` creates a directory at the scratchpad's path.

## Affected code

`src/library.ts` — the three producers of a path, and the guard present in only two of them:

```ts
// rename()  -- GUARDED
if (next === this.scratchpadPath())
  throw new Error("That title is reserved for the scratchpad.");

// move()  -- GUARDED
if (next === this.scratchpadPath())
  throw new Error("That filename is reserved for the scratchpad.");

// createCollection()  -- NO GUARD
async createCollection(name: string): Promise<void> {
  const safe = name.trim().replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, "-");
  if (!safe) throw new Error("Enter a collection name.");
  await this.ensureFolder(`${this.folder()}/${safe}`);   // <-- may occupy the scratchpad path
  this.emit();
}
```

The reservation is clearly intended — two of the three producers implement it — so
`createCollection` is the one path that bypasses it.

`contains()` is also name-equality-only, so it does not help:

```ts
contains = (path: string): boolean => {
  const folder = this.folder();
  return (
    path.startsWith(`${folder}/`) &&
    path.endsWith(".md") &&
    path !== `${folder}/${SCRATCHPAD_NAME}`     // exact path only, not descendants
  );
};
```

### Library-layer consequences (executed — see Evidence)

Once a folder occupies the path, both scratchpad entry points fail:

```ts
async readScratchpad(path: string): Promise<string> {
  const file = this.app.vault.getAbstractFileByPath(path);
  if (!file) return "";
  if (!(file instanceof TFile)) throw new Error("The scratchpad path is not a Markdown file.");
  return run(() => this.app.vault.read(file));
}
```

`getAbstractFileByPath` now resolves to a `TFolder`, so the `instanceof TFile` guard throws, and
`saveScratchpad` throws the identical message.

## Impact

- **The scratchpad is dead for the session, with no self-heal.** `collections()` now lists the
  folder, so the row is visible but the file is not a file. Recovery requires renaming or deleting
  the folder outside the app (in Obsidian's file explorer) — there is no in-app path out.
- **A phantom collection appears in the sidebar** with a count of 0 fragments, presented exactly
  like a real collection.
- The failure is **silent at creation time**: the dialog reports success.

### App-layer consequence (static analysis — not executed; see Evidence)

`useScratchpad` in `src/app.tsx` has no recovery path for a failed *read*:

```ts
void library
  .readScratchpad(path)
  .then((loaded) => { current.ready = true; setText(loaded); setStatus("saved"); })
  .catch((error: Error) => { setStatus("error"); errorNotice(error); });   // current.ready stays false
```

and the editor is still enabled, because the textarea is disabled only while *loading*:

```tsx
<textarea disabled={status === "loading"} value={text} onChange={(event) => onChange(event.target.value)} ... />
```

so on the read failure the user gets an **enabled, focusable, caret-showing textarea that silently
discards every keystroke**:

```ts
const editScratchpad = (value: string): void => {
  const current = session.current;
  if (!current?.ready) return;   // <-- returns BEFORE setText; nothing is echoed and nothing is stored
  ...
};
```

The status reads **"Could not save"**, although nothing was ever saved — the failure was a *read*.
The user is told the wrong thing, and the field looks fully functional.

## Reproduction (deterministic)

The real `src/library.ts`, bundled with esbuild from `src/`, with `obsidian` aliased to a stub
implementing the documented contracts for `normalizePath` / `getFrontMatterInfo` / `TFile` / `TFolder`
and an in-memory vault. No React.

```js
const lib = new FragmentLibrary(app, { folder: "Fragments" });
await lib.load();
await lib.createCollection("_fragments-scratchpad.md");
```

Observed:

```
collections() before : []
createCollection('_fragments-scratchpad.md') -> OK   (no error shown to the user)
folder now occupies the scratchpad path: true
collections() after  : [ '_fragments-scratchpad.md' ]   <-- phantom row in the sidebar
readScratchpad       -> THROWS: The scratchpad path is not a Markdown file.
saveScratchpad       -> THROWS: The scratchpad path is not a Markdown file.
```

### Control — the same name IS reserved by `rename()`

```
rename("Fragments/real.md", "_fragments-scratchpad")
  -> REJECTED: That title is reserved for the scratchpad.   <-- guard fires here
```

Identical target name, same session, same library: `rename` refuses it, `createCollection` accepts
it. This isolates the defect to the missing guard rather than to the input or the sanitiser.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** a collection name that would occupy the scratchpad's path is refused with a clear
  message, exactly as `rename()` and `move()` already do. The scratchpad cannot be silently
  disabled from the UI.
- **Actual:** the collection is created, a phantom folder and sidebar row appear, and the
  scratchpad's read and write both throw for the rest of the session, leaving an enabled editor that
  silently discards input while reporting "Could not save".

## Suggested fix

Apply the existing reservation check in `createCollection`, comparing the resolved folder path
against `this.scratchpadPath()` before calling `ensureFolder`:

```ts
async createCollection(name: string): Promise<void> {
  const safe = name.trim().replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, "-");
  if (!safe) throw new Error("Enter a collection name.");
  if (`${this.folder()}/${safe}` === this.scratchpadPath())
    throw new Error("That name is reserved for the scratchpad.");
  await this.ensureFolder(`${this.folder()}/${safe}`);
  this.emit();
}
```

Better still, centralise the reservation so all three producers share one predicate. Separately,
`useScratchpad` should distinguish a read failure from a write failure and should re-arm (or
disable) the textarea when `ready` is false, rather than leaving an enabled field that drops input.

## Relationship to existing issues

- `fragments-createcollection-flattens-nested-paths-4ht` is also in `createCollection`, but concerns
  `/` being flattened to `-` and producing two spellings of one name. This report is about the
  **absent reserved-name check** and its effect on the scratchpad; fixing the flattening does not add
  the guard.
- `fragments-e1h` is about the `conflicted` latch set by a failing **write**, and its proposed fix
  (re-read and reset `current.saved` / `current.conflicted`) does **not** help here: this failure is a
  **read**, so `current.ready` is never set and `editScratchpad` returns before any conflicted check.
- `fragments-s6k` is in `move()` and concerns a filename clash being reported as a title clash.

## Evidence

- Library layer (read/save both throw, phantom collection row, `rename` control): **executed** with

Vault seeded with a normal fragment plus a folder occupying the scratchpad path:

- `Fragments/Alpha.md` (so a fragment is selected and the scratchpad pane renders)
- `Fragments/_fragments-scratchpad.md/Untitled fragment.md` (makes that path a **folder** on disk)

`createCollection("_fragments-scratchpad.md")` is not even needed in this run — any path that leaves a
folder at the scratchpad location triggers it. Then `<AppShell/>` is mounted with
`react-dom/client`, effects are allowed to settle, and a keystroke is delivered the way a user
delivers one (native value setter + bubbling `input` event, which is what React's `onChange`
observes):

```
=== 07y APP-LAYER: executed against the real AppShell ===
scratchpad textarea present : true
status text                 : "Could not save"
textarea disabled?          : false   <-- false means the user can focus/type
textarea value before typing : ""
textarea value AFTER typing  : ""      <-- empty means the keystroke was dropped
status text after typing    : "Could not save"

status mislabels a READ failure as a SAVE failure: YES
```
