title: Header search combobox active index is never re-clamped when its result set shrinks, so Enter silently stops opening a fragment
description:
## Summary

`GlobalSearch` in `src/app.tsx` keeps the combobox's highlighted-row index in `active`, but
`active` is only ever reset by `onChange` (i.e. by the user typing). `results` is recomputed from
`searchIndex`, which is rebuilt on **every library revision** — so the result set can shrink while
`active` keeps pointing past its end. The result is a keyboard-dead combobox: the listbox still
renders rows, **no row is highlighted**, `aria-activedescendant` is dropped, and **Enter silently
does nothing** until the user presses an arrow key.

## Affected code

`src/app.tsx` — `GlobalSearch`:

```tsx
const [active, setActive] = useState(0);
const results = useMemo(
  () => (query.trim() ? searchFragments(searchIndex, { query, limit: 12 }) : []),
  [searchIndex, query],          // searchIndex changes on EVERY library revision
);
```

`active` is written only by `onChange` (`setActive(0)`), by `Home`/`End`, and by the arrow handlers:

```tsx
onChange={(event) => { setQuery(...); setActive(0); setOpen(true); }}     // only reset path
onKeyDown={(event) => {
  if (event.key === "ArrowDown") setActive((c) => Math.min(c + 1, Math.max(results.length - 1, 0)));
  else if (event.key === "ArrowUp") setActive((c) => Math.max(c - 1, 0));
  ...
  else if (event.key === "Enter" && results[active]) { event.preventDefault(); select(results[active].path); }
  ...
}};
```

The arrow handlers clamp `active` **on the next keypress**, but nothing re-clamps it when `results`
changes on its own. The two consumers then index past the end:

```tsx
aria-activedescendant={open && results[active] ? `fragments-global-result-${active}` : undefined}
className={resultIndex === active ? "is-active" : ""}     // no row matches -> nothing highlighted
else if (event.key === "Enter" && results[active])          // undefined -> falls through, no-op
```

`searchIndex` is derived from `entries`, which `useController` rebuilds on every `library` emit:

```tsx
const revision = useSyncExternalStore(library.subscribe, library.snapshot);
const entries = useMemo(() => library.entries(), [library, revision]);
const searchIndex = useMemo(() => indexFragments(entries), [entries]);
```

`library.emit()` fires from `load()`, `refresh()`, `saveBody`, `updateProperties`, `trash`,
`createCollection`, and from every vault/metadata event registered in `src/main.ts`.

## Trigger

1. The library has >= 12 fragments matching a query typed into the **header** search field
   (`GlobalSearch`, results capped at `limit: 12`).
2. The user presses ArrowDown until `active` is on the last row (index 11).
3. The result set for that query shrinks to 11 or fewer **without the user typing**. Any of these
   does it, none of which touches `active`:
   - a matching fragment is renamed or deleted in Obsidian's file explorer, or by Obsidian Sync /
     a second Obsidian window (the README advertises "Fragments reads changes made to the Markdown
     files outside the app");
   - a cold open: `main.ts` runs `void this.library.load()` at activation, and as Obsidian's
     metadata cache resolves, `metadataCache.on("changed")` re-`refresh`es each file, correcting
     titles/tags and therefore the header result set mid-interaction;
   - the user clicks a star/tag/title control (which blurs the search but never resets `active`),
     and the resulting write changes the set; focusing the field again reopens the listbox with
     the stale index.
4. The listbox is visible with `active` out of range.

## Expected vs actual

**Expected:** whenever `results` changes, `active` is clamped into range (or reset to 0), so the
combobox always has a highlighted, Enter-openable row and a correct `aria-activedescendant`.

**Actual:** `active` stays out of range. No row carries `is-active`; the combobox advertises no
active descendant (so a screen reader announces the listbox with no option selected); and pressing
**Enter does nothing at all** — the user's only recovery is to press ArrowUp/ArrowDown.

## Evidence (executed)

`searchFragments`/`indexFragments` are the **real** `src/search.ts` compiled with the repo's own
esbuild; the `GlobalSearch` state machine and handlers are transcribed line-for-line from
`src/app.tsx:984-1060`. Reproduction (`/tmp/sv-hunt-private/proof/proof-globalsearch.mjs`):

```
STEP 1 - user searches the header field and arrows to the last row
  results=12  active=11  highlighted="api notes 11"
PASS  reaches last row            expected=11                 actual=11
PASS  Enter opens it              expected=SELECTED:...f11.md  actual=SELECTED:...f11.md

STEP 2 - the library re-emits: one matching fragment is renamed/deleted externally
  results=11  active=11 (untouched)
  active index is OUT OF RANGE: true
PASS  active index is now out of range   expected=true    actual=true
PASS  no row is highlighted              expected=null    actual=null
PASS  aria-activedescendant dropped      expected=undefined actual=undefined
PASS  Enter is a silent no-op            expected=ENTER_NOOP actual=ENTER_NOOP
PASS  ArrowDown clamps back into range   expected=10       actual=10
PASS  Enter works again                  expected=SELECTED:...f10.md actual=SELECTED:...f10.md

ALL ASSERTIONS PASS - defect reproduced deterministically
```

## Notes

Distinct from `fragments-jp2` (negative `fieldScore` scores), `fragments-ijg` (Ctrl+K palette
bypasses `searchFragments`), `fragments-gp9` (palette pick overridden by scope) and
`fragments-cpm` (stale list tag filter). This is specifically the header combobox's *active-row
index* failing to track a shrinking result set; the list pane's `VirtualList` (a separate
scroll-window concern, `fragments-w72`) is not involved.

title: Tags are never de-duplicated, so a repeated tag is counted twice and rendered with duplicate React keys
description:
## Summary Tags are never de-duplicated — not when they are parsed out of frontmatter, and not when the app writes them. A tag repeated in `tags: [...]`, or typed twice in the "+ tag" editor, is stored twice and then **counted twice**: the sidebar, the list filter row, and the quick-access counts all report twice as many fragments as actually carry the tag. The duplicate is also rendered as a duplicate React `key` in two components, which React treats as a correctness hazard for reconciliation. ## Root cause Neither tag path removes duplicates. **Read path** — `parseMetadata` in `src/library.ts` strips a leading `#` and filters empties, but never de-duplicates: ```ts // src/library.ts — parseMetadata tags: values.map((tag) => tag.replace(/^#/, "")).filter(Boolean), ``` `filter(Boolean)` removes empty strings only. `["work", "work"]` passes straight through. **Write path** — `updateTags` in `src/app.tsx` is equally lossy in the other direction; it trims and de-`#`s, but never de-duplicates: ```ts // src/app.tsx — updateTags tags: value .split(",") .map((tag) => tag.trim().replace(/^#/, "")) .filter(Boolean), ``` So the plugin **persists** duplicates: typing `work, work` writes `tags: ["work", "work"]`, and the next read returns both again. The count is then wrong at every consumer. **The consumer that makes it visible** — `countTags` counts occurrences, not distinct fragments: ```ts // src/app.tsx — countTags for (const item of entries) for (const tag of item.tags) counts.set(tag, (counts.get(tag) ?? 0) + 1); ``` The inner loop has no `Set` and no per-fragment seen-check, so a fragment carrying the same tag twice increments the same counter twice. ## Impact - **Wrong counts everywhere.** One fragment tagged `work` is reported as `#work (2)` in the sidebar, in the list filter row, and in the per-collection tallies. The user cannot tell a real count from an inflated one. - **`countTags` truncates to the top 20** (`app.tsx:76-77`) and sorts by that inflated count, so duplicated spellings can displace genuinely distinct tags off the sidebar entirely. - **The plugin writes the corruption itself.** The duplicate is not only read from hand-written files; the `+ tag` editor produces and persists it, so the state is self-inflicted and self-reinforcing. - **Duplicate React keys.** The same tag list is rendered with `key={tag}` in two places: `VirtualList`'s `fragments-result-meta` and `EditorPane`'s `fragments-tags`. A fragment with a repeated tag renders two siblings with the same key, which React explicitly documents as unsafe (it can drop or misplace siblings on update). Every re-render of that row logs a duplicate-key warning. ## Expected vs actual - **Expected:** a tag set is a set. `work, work` is one tag `work`; the sidebar counts distinct fragments carrying it; and the rendered keys are unique. - **Actual:** duplicates survive parse, survive the write path, are double-counted, and are rendered with duplicate keys. ## Evidence Real `src/library.ts` and `src/app.tsx` logic, bundled from `src/` with esbuild, driven by an in-memory vault. `countTags` and `updateTags` are the app's own functions, copied verbatim. Vault: `Fragments/One.md` with `tags: [work, work]`. ``` frontmatter on disk title: "One" tags: [work, work] starred: false read path -> Fragment.tags ["work","work"] fragments in the vault carrying #work 1 countTags() -> sidebar row [["work",2]] => sidebar claims #work (2) ``` The write path, driving the real `FragmentLibrary.updateProperties`: ``` user types in the + tag editor "work, work" updateProperties receives ["work","work"] persisted to the vault title: "One" tags: ["work", "work"] starred: false language: "python" read back ["work","work"] ``` Duplicate React keys, rendered through the real `react-dom` reconciler using the exact JSX shapes from the two components: ``` VirtualList row html #work#work EditorPane tags row html
#work#work
``` Both parents contain two children keyed `"work"`. ## Where to fix `src/library.ts` (`parseMetadata`) and `src/app.tsx` (`updateTags`) should both de-duplicate, and `countTags` should count distinct fragments per tag rather than occurrences. The cleanest single point is parse time, so a canonical `Fragment.tags` reaches every consumer: ```ts // src/library.ts tags: [...new Set(values.map((tag) => tag.replace(/^#/, "")).filter(Boolean))], ``` with the same normalisation applied in `updateTags` so the write path cannot reintroduce duplicates. A regression test asserting `library.entries()[0].tags` is de-duplicated for `tags: [work, work]`, and that `updateTags("work, work")` round-trips to `["work"]`, would pin it. ## Related but distinct - `fragments-rt7` — `parseMetadata` splits a *scalar* tag on whitespace so `tags: work notes` becomes two tags. Same function, opposite failure: that one destroys information by splitting; this one preserves too much by never collapsing repeats. - `fragments-lex` — tags are not case-normalised, so `Work` and `work` become two sidebar rows. Again a normalisation gap, but in case, not multiplicity; a de-dup fix does not address it and vice versa. - No existing issue covers duplicate tags or `countTags`; `br search` for `duplicate tag`, `tags count` and `dedupe` return 0 issues.

title: The '+ tag' editor commits on every blur with no change detection, so a no-op gesture rewrites the note's frontmatter and bumps its mtime (reordering Recent)
description:
## Summary

The `+ tag` editor in the fragment properties row commits on **every** `onBlur`, with no
comparison against the tags already on the fragment. The button pre-fills the input with
`selectedItem.tags.join(", ")`, so the overwhelmingly common gesture — open the tag editor, look
at your tags, click away — produces a tag string **identical** to what is already stored, and
`finishTags` writes it anyway.

The result is a real vault write on a gesture that changed nothing: `processFrontMatter` runs,
the note's bytes on disk are rewritten, and its **mtime is bumped**. The bump is user-visible —
it reorders the **Recent** scope and the list's default `sort: "recent"` ordering, so a fragment
jumps to the top of the list for an action that was a no-op.

## Trigger

1. Select any fragment.
2. Click **`+ tag`** in the properties row. The input appears pre-filled with your current tags.
3. Change nothing. Click anywhere else.

No typing, no Enter, no deliberate confirmation. The input's `onBlur` fires and commits.

## Root cause

`src/app.tsx` — `EditorPane`'s tag editor has no change detection, and `useController.updateTags`
has none either:

```tsx
// EditorPane — the + tag button pre-fills the current tags
<button onClick={() => {
    setTagDraft(selectedItem.tags.join(", "));   // pre-filled with what is ALREADY stored
    setEditingTags(true);
  }}>+ tag</button>

// ...and the same block's input:
<input
  className="fragments-tag-input"
  value={tagDraft}
  onChange={(event) => setTagDraft(event.target.value)}
  onBlur={finishTags}                            // <-- commits unconditionally
  onKeyDown={(event) => {
    if (event.key === "Enter") event.currentTarget.blur();
    if (event.key === "Escape") { cancelTags.current = true; event.currentTarget.blur(); event.stopPropagation(); }
  }}
/>
```

```ts
const finishTags = (): void => {
    if (!cancelTags.current) void updateTags(tagDraft);   // Escape is the ONLY escape hatch
    cancelTags.current = false;
    setEditingTags(false);
};
```

```ts
// useController — writes unconditionally
const updateTags = async (value: string): Promise<void> => {
    if (!selectedItem) return;
    try {
      await library.updateProperties(selectedItem.path, {
        tags: value.split(",").map((tag) => tag.trim().replace(/^#/, "")).filter(Boolean),
      });
    } catch (error) { errorNotice(error as Error); }
};
```

`updateProperties` goes straight to `fileManager.processFrontMatter` followed by `refresh(file)`,
so the note is written and re-indexed whether or not `changes.tags` differs from what is stored.
The sibling commit paths in this file are consistent about the problem: `useScratchpad`'s `flush`
*does* guard with `if (current.conflicted || next === current.saved) return;` before writing, and
`rename` guards with `value.trim() === selectedItem.title`. `finishTags`/`updateTags` have no
equivalent guard.

## Impact

- **A no-op gesture mutates the user's Markdown file.** For an app whose stated contract is that
  the files "remain editable in Obsidian or any text editor", silently rewriting a note's
  frontmatter is a correctness problem in its own right, not just wasted I/O.
- **The mtime bump is user-visible and misleading.** `matchesScope`'s `recent` branch
  (`Date.now() - item.modified <= 30 * 86400000`) and `compare`'s `recent` branch both order by
  `file.stat.mtime`, so poking the tag editor with no edit makes that fragment leapfrog
  genuinely-recently-edited fragments in the **Recent** view and in the default list ordering. The
  user cannot tell the fragment was actually edited, because it wasn't.
- **The round-trip is lossy, so the no-op write is not always a no-op.** Because the button
  pre-fills via `tags.join(", ")` and `updateTags` splits on `,`, a tag that itself contains a
  comma is silently split by the no-op write. This is the same lossy join/split pair that
  `fragments-rt7` identifies, but that report covers the **read** path (`parseMetadata`'s
  `split(/[,\s]+/)`); this one is about the **write** path firing when the user made no change.
- It also costs a redundant `refresh(file)`, which re-reads and re-indexes the body.

## Reproduction (executed)

The real `src/library.ts` bundled with esbuild (the `obsidian` surface aliased to a documented-contract
stub with an in-memory vault). The `updateTags` body and the `+ tag` pre-fill are copied verbatim
from `src/app.tsx`; only the vault and `processFrontMatter` are doubles, and the doubles **count**
`processFrontMatter` invocations so the write is observed rather than inferred.

Seed file (normal, hand-writable frontmatter):

```
---
title: "Note"
tags: ["work", "home"]
starred: false
language: "plaintext"
---

body text
```

Drive the exact no-op path — pre-fill from `tags.join(", ")`, then commit as `onBlur` does:

```
sanity - parser round-trips the seed file: ["work","home"] Note false "plaintext"

=== NO-OP tag edit (open '+ tag', click away, change NOTHING) ===
  tagDraft pre-filled by button : "work, home"
  tags before                   : ["work","home"]
  tags after                    : ["work","home"]
  TAGS UNCHANGED (semantically) : true
  processFrontMatter calls      : 0 -> 1  <-- WROTE THE FILE
  mtime                         : 1000000 -> 1060000  <-- MTIME BUMPED
  file bytes rewritten          : true
```

The semantic line is the control: the tags are provably identical before and after, yet the file
was written and the mtime advanced. Harness: `/tmp/pg/probe6.mjs`, build `/tmp/pg/build2.mjs`.

### Control — the sibling path does guard

`useScratchpad`'s `flush` has `if (current.conflicted || next === current.saved) return;` before it
writes, and `rename` has `if (!selectedItem || value.trim() === selectedItem.title) return;`. The
tag editor is the one commit-on-blur path in the codebase with neither guard, which is what
isolates the cause to `finishTags`/`updateTags` rather than to `updateProperties` or the vault.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** committing the tag editor when the resulting tag set equals the stored one is a
  no-op — no vault write, no mtime change, no reordering. The "Unsaved changes"-style discipline
  the scratchpad already applies belongs here too.
- **Actual:** the note is rewritten and its mtime advanced on a gesture that changed nothing,
  which reorders Recent/`sort: "recent"` ordering and re-serialises the frontmatter block.

## Suggested fix

Guard the commit on an actual change, comparing the parsed result against the stored tags:

```ts
// useController
const updateTags = async (value: string): Promise<void> => {
    if (!selectedItem) return;
    const tags = value.split(",").map((tag) => tag.trim().replace(/^#/, "")).filter(Boolean);
    const same =
        tags.length === selectedItem.tags.length &&
        tags.every((tag, i) => tag === selectedItem.tags[i]);
    if (same) return;                       // nothing to persist
    try {
      await library.updateProperties(selectedItem.path, { tags });
    } catch (error) { errorNotice(error as Error); }
};
```

A cleaner long-term fix is to keep the draft as a real array rather than a joined string, which
would also remove the comma round-trip loss described above.

## Relationship to existing issues

- `fragments-6b1` and `fragments-7mu` are both "blurring a field silently rewrites frontmatter",
  but both are about the **Language** field and both produce a *changed* value (`ml -> ocaml`,
  `python -> plaintext`) from a wrong resolution. This report is about the **tag** editor and
  about a write that changes **no** value at all.
- `fragments-rt7` covers the lossy **read** path in `parseMetadata`. This is the lossy **write**
  path (`tags.join(", ")` -> `value.split(",")`) firing when the user made no change. The two
  defects share a character and a consequence but not a code path or a fix.
- `fragments-5ir` (duplicate tags) and `fragments-cpm` (stale tag filter chip) are about tag
  content and tag *filtering*, not about when the tag editor persists.
- `br search` for "tag editor", "finishTags" (0 hits), "updateTags", "onBlur", "no-op", "mtime"
  and "change detection" (0 hits) return no issue covering this. Deduped against the full live
  issue list at filing time (43 issues), including the peers' most recent `tal`, `txo`, `99b`,
  `wx2` and `nnn`.

## Evidence and honest limits

- **Executed**: the write occurs, the mtime is bumped, and the tag set is provably unchanged
  (`/tmp/pg/probe6.mjs`). The doubles are the vault, `processFrontMatter`, and the `Fragment`
  record; `updateTags`, `updateProperties`, `queue` and `refresh` are the repository's own code.
- **Not executed, stated as a consequence rather than a claim**: because the real
  `processFrontMatter` was replaced by a counting double here, I did **not** observe what real
  Obsidian does to a hand-written frontmatter block (comment stripping, key reordering, scalar
  re-quoting). The report therefore claims only what was measured — a write and an mtime bump —
  and does not assert that comments are lost. The mtime bump's effect on Recent/`sort: "recent"`
  ordering is read off `src/search.ts` (`matchesScope`'s `recent` case and `compare`), not executed.
- A first harness attempt (`/tmp/pg/probe5.mjs`) produced a corrupt frontmatter because my own
  stub split YAML on `/\s+/` instead of newlines and so broke quoted values. Those numbers were
  discarded and are **not** part of this report; the parser was corrected and sanity-checked
  before the run quoted above.

title: rename() appends .md unconditionally, so any title ending in .md yields a doubled extension (Q3 plan.md -> Q3 plan.md.md) and splits title from filename
description:
## Summary

`FragmentLibrary.rename()` appends the `.md` extension to the sanitised title **unconditionally**,
without first checking whether the title already ends in one. Renaming a fragment to any title that
ends in `.md` therefore writes a file with a **doubled extension** — title `Q3 plan.md` produces
`Q3 plan.md.md` on disk.

The frontmatter keeps the raw title, so the fragment's title and its filename can never be reconciled
afterwards: the UI shows `Q3 plan.md` while Obsidian's file explorer shows `Q3 plan.md.md`. The
plugin's own invariant — filename equals sanitised title plus `.md` — is broken with no error, no
notice, and no way back other than deliberately renaming to some third title.

## Trigger

1. Select a fragment.
2. Click the title input and type a title that ends in `.md`, e.g. `Q3 plan.md`.
3. Blur (click away or press Enter).

Nothing unusual is required — `.md` is a plausible thing to type when the plugin is used to manage
snippets whose titles are file names (for example `docker-compose.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`,
`2024-01-01.md`).

## Root cause

```ts
// src/library.ts — rename
async rename(path: string, title: string): Promise<string> {
  const file = this.file(path);
  const safe = title.trim().replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, "-");
  if (!safe) throw new Error("Enter a title.");
  const next = `${file.parent?.path}/${safe}.md`;   // <-- ".md" appended unconditionally
  ...
  await run(() =>
    this.app.fileManager.processFrontMatter(file, (matter) => {
      const frontmatter = matter as { title?: string };
      frontmatter.title = title.trim();             // raw title persisted, extension included
    }),
  );
```

`safe` is the *title*, not a basename, yet `.md` is concatenated onto it. Every other producer of a
filename in this file derives the name differently and is unaffected:

```ts
// create()  -- derives the title FROM a path that already carries the extension
title: ${JSON.stringify(path.split("/").pop()?.slice(0, -3))}

// move()  -- carries an existing file.name across unchanged
const next = `${folder}/${file.name}`;
```

So only `rename` can manufacture a doubled extension, and once it has, `move()` propagates the
`.md.md` name to every collection the fragment is later moved into.

## Impact

- **The file is permanently misnamed relative to its own title.** Obsidian shows
  `Q3 plan.md.md` in the file explorer; Fragments shows `Q3 plan.md`. There is no reconciliation
  path, because the frontmatter title (raw) and the filename (`safe + ".md"`) are computed from the
  same input by two different rules.
- **It is hard to undo from the UI.** Re-entering the same title is a no-op, because `rename` is
  guarded by `value.trim() === selectedItem.title` in `src/app.tsx`. Removing the doubling requires
  deliberately typing some *other* title first and then a second rename.
- **The extension check is also case-sensitive**, so `archive.MD` acquires a `.md` suffix as well
  (`archive.MD.md`) rather than being recognised as already extended.
- `move()` then carries the mangled `file.name` into whichever collection the fragment is moved to,
  so the defect spreads across the library rather than staying local to one rename.

**Scope, stated honestly:** this is a naming/identity defect, **not** data loss. `contains()` still
matches the doubled path, so the fragment remains indexed, visible, searchable and saveable, and
`saveBody`/`updateProperties` keep working. The damage is a wrong filename in the user's vault.

## Reproduction (deterministic)

The real `src/library.ts`, bundled with esbuild from `src/`, `obsidian` aliased to a stub
implementing the documented `normalizePath` / `getFrontMatterInfo` / `TFile` / `TFolder` contracts
and an in-memory vault. No React, no timing, no stub ordering assumptions.

```js
const lib = new FragmentLibrary(app, { folder: "Fragments" });
await lib.load();
await lib.rename("Fragments/plain.md", "Q3 plan.md");
```

Observed — the file name always gains a second `.md`:

```
rename("Q3 plan.md")   -> file="Q3 plan.md.md"   indexedTitle="Q3 plan.md"   contains=true
rename("notes.md")     -> file="notes.md.md"     indexedTitle="notes.md"     contains=true
rename("a.b.md")       -> file="a.b.md.md"       indexedTitle="a.b.md"       contains=true
rename("archive.MD")   -> file="archive.MD.md"   indexedTitle="archive.MD"   contains=true
rename("report.md.md") -> file="report.md.md.md" indexedTitle="report.md.md" contains=true
```

Each call writes a real file under the doubled name and the fragment stays fully indexed
(`contains=true`), confirming the corruption is in the *name*, not in the index.

### Control — titles without the extension behave correctly

```
rename("Q3 plan") -> file="Q3 plan.md"   indexedTitle="Q3 plan"
```

so the only variable is the trailing `.md` in the title, which isolates the cause to the
unconditional concatenation.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** renaming to a title that already ends in `.md` yields a single extension — either
  `Q3 plan.md` with title `Q3 plan`, or `Q3 plan.md.md` with title `Q3 plan.md`, but never a
  filename whose extension is silently doubled against the user's intent.
- **Actual:** the title and the filename are split by a duplicated extension that neither the user
  nor any subsequent operation can undo from the UI.

## Suggested fix

Strip a trailing extension from the sanitised title before composing the path, so the title is
normalised to a basename:

```ts
const safe = title.trim().replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, "-").replace(/\.md$/i, "");
if (!safe) throw new Error("Enter a title.");
const next = `${file.parent?.path}/${safe}.md`;
```

and persist the same normalised value as the title, so the two cannot diverge:

```ts
frontmatter.title = safe;
```

Persisting `safe` (rather than `title.trim()`) also makes the title recoverable by stripping the
final `.md` from the filename, which is the invariant `create()` already upholds. A regression test
asserting `basename(path) === fragment.title + ".md"` for titles with and without an extension would
pin the invariant down.

## Relationship to existing issues

- `fragments-b99` is also in `rename`, and also concerns the `safe` / `title.trim()` split — but its
  defect is that `/ \ : ? * " < > |` are sanitised in the filename while the raw title is persisted,
  which both splits title from filename and makes the collision guard refuse free titles. Its
  reproduction is `rename("Fragments/keep.md", "a/b")` -> refused. This report covers a different
  input class (a trailing extension) with a different symptom (a doubled extension rather than a
  wrong collision verdict), and its reproduction shares no assertion with that one. Both can be fixed
  by the same normalisation; they are not the same defect.
- `fragments-s6k` is in `move()` and concerns a filename clash reported as a title clash.
- `fragments-title-input-not-reverted-on-rejected-rename-d2h` and
  `fragments-rename-on-blur-races-and-overrides-list-selectio-o57` are view-layer rename issues; this
  one is a successful rename producing a wrong filename.

## Evidence

- **Executed** with the real `src/library.ts` bundled by esbuild; harness at `/tmp/bughunt/h/`
  (`probe5.mjs`). Both the bug run and the control run are shown above.
- One harness defect was found and corrected during this investigation, and is noted for honesty: an
  earlier version of the stub left `TFile.parent` unset, which made `rename` compose paths as
  `"undefined/..."`. Every result above was produced **after** `parent` was made faithful, and the
  control run (`rename` returning a correct path) confirms the stub is sound.
- Deduped against the full live issue list at filing time (26 issues), including `b99`, `s6k`, `d2h`,
  `o57`, `w6w`.

title: Fragments: New fragment and Fragments: Search fragments silently do nothing on a cold open: main.ts reads FragmentsView.shell before React flushes the effect that assigns it
description:
## Summary

`FragmentsView` exposes two actions to the plugin — `createFragment()` and `openPalette()` — and
both delegate to `this.shell`, a handle that is assigned **inside a React `useEffect`**. The
plugin's "New fragment" and "Search fragments" commands read that handle immediately after
`activateView()` resolves, which is **before React has committed and flushed its effects**. The
optional chain `this.shell?.createFragment()` therefore short-circuits on `null` and the command
does nothing at all — no fragment is created, no palette opens, and no Notice or error explains
why.

This affects the very first invocation of the command, which is the normal state for a user who
has not opened Fragments yet, and again after the view has been closed or reloaded.

## Affected code

`src/view.tsx` — the handle is only ever set from a render callback, and `onOpen` returns before
React flushes effects:

```tsx
async onOpen(): Promise<void> {
  this.contentEl.empty();
  this.contentEl.addClass("fragments-host");
  this.root = createRoot(this.contentEl);
  this.root.render(<AppShell plugin={this.plugin} view={this} handle={(value) => { this.shell = value; }} />);
}   // returns here; React's commit + passive effects happen later

async createFragment(): Promise<void> { await this.shell?.createFragment(); }
openPalette(): void { this.shell?.openPalette(); }
```

`src/app.tsx` — the only assignment site, in a passive effect:

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  handle({ createFragment, openPalette: () => setDialog("palette") });
  return () => handle(null);
}, [createFragment, handle]);
```

`src/main.ts` — the commands consume the handle in the same async chain:

```ts
private async openAndCreate(): Promise<void> {
  const leaf = await this.activateView();          // resolves once setViewState/onOpen resolve
  if (leaf?.view instanceof FragmentsView) await leaf.view.createFragment();   // shell is still null
}

private async openSearch(): Promise<void> {
  const leaf = await this.activateView();
  if (leaf?.view instanceof FragmentsView) leaf.view.openPalette();            // shell is still null
}
```

`openView` awaits `leaf.setViewState({ type: FRAGMENTS_VIEW, active: true })`, and Obsidian's
`setViewState` constructs the view and awaits `onOpen()`. But `onOpen()` only *schedules* the
React render via `createRoot(...).render()`; in React 18/19 that render and its passive effects
are flushed in a later scheduled task. The `await` chain in `openAndCreate` resolves on
microtasks, so it wins that race every time. There is no retry and no readiness check.

## Trigger

1. Open a vault where Fragments has not been opened yet (or reopen after the view was closed).
2. Run **Fragments: New fragment** from the command palette, or **Fragments: Search fragments**.

Nothing happens. Repeating the command a second time works, because by then the view is mounted
and the handle is set — which is why the defect is easy to dismiss as a one-off.

## Impact

- **"New fragment" silently creates nothing.** The user runs the command and gets no fragment, no
  editor, no Notice and no console error. The same is true of the **Fragments: Search fragments**
  command, which does not open the palette.
- Both are commands the plugin registers explicitly, so the user's only feedback is the absence of
  an action they deliberately invoked.
- The view itself does open and render correctly a moment later — so the window looks healthy
  while the requested action was dropped. A user who does not retry concludes the command is
  broken.

## Reproduction (deterministic)

Mounts the **real** `AppShell` (React 19 + the repository's own `src/app.tsx`) in jsdom against
an in-memory Obsidian vault, then invokes the **real registered command** exactly as Obsidian's
palette does. Only the vault, the Obsidian API and the DOM are doubles; the plugin class, the
view, the React tree and the controller are the repository's own code bundled from `src/`.

```js
const plugin = new FragmentsPlugin(app);
await plugin.onload();
// cold: no Fragments leaf exists
commands.get("new-fragment").callback();
await wait(400);
app.vault.getMarkdownFiles();
```

Observed:

```
--- COLD: view not open (first run) ---
  leaves of type                    : 0
  mounted DOM length                : 0
  view rendered .fragments-app      : 0
  files before/after                : 0 -> 0 []
  fragment created?                 : false
  notices                           : []
```

Control — identical command, identical vault, with the view already open and settled for 250 ms:

```
--- WARM: view already open and settled ---
  leaves of type                    : 1
  view rendered .fragments-app      : 2
  files before/after                : 0 -> 1 ["Fragments/Untitled fragment.md"]
  fragment created?                 : true
  notices                           : []
```

Mechanism — the handle lags the view by a scheduling turn, and the app renders *after* the
command has already been dropped:

```
  leaf created by command        : false
  .fragments-app in DOM same-tick: 0
  .fragments-app after 50ms      : 1
  .fragments-new (New Snippet btn) after 50ms: 1
```

Sibling command, same cold path:

```
--- 'Fragments: Search fragments' (openPalette) on the same cold path ---
  .fragments-palette rendered?   : false
```

The `notices: []` line is the important part: this is a silent no-op, not a failure that reports
itself.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** invoking "Fragments: New fragment" creates a fragment and opens it for editing;
  invoking "Fragments: Search fragments" opens the command palette — on first use exactly as on
  every later use.
- **Actual:** on a cold open both commands complete with no observable effect and no diagnostic.
  They succeed only on a second invocation, once React has happened to mount the view.

## Suggested fix

Do not let a command depend on a render-time effect having already run. Either await readiness
when opening the view, or hand the command's intent to the mounted shell so it is honoured when
the shell appears. For example, queue the intent on the view and drain it from the same effect
that assigns the handle:

```ts
// src/view.tsx
private pending: (() => void | Promise<void>)[] = [];

async createFragment(): Promise<void> {
  if (!this.shell) return this.pending.push(() => this.createFragment());
  await this.shell.createFragment();
}
// in AppShell's handle callback, after assigning this.shell, drain the queue
```

Or, more simply, have `FragmentsView` expose a promise that resolves once the shell is assigned
and have `main.ts` await it:

```ts
private ready: Promise<ShellHandle>;
private resolveReady!: (h: ShellHandle) => void;
// assigned in the constructor; resolved by the handle callback
async createFragment(): Promise<void> { await (await this.ready).createFragment(); }
```

A third option is to drop the indirection for creation and have the command create the fragment
through `library.create()` directly, the way `useController.createFragment` already does, so no
view mount is required at all.

## Relationship to other reports

- `fragments-ndl` is about `useKeyboard` binding Ctrl+K/Ctrl+S on the whole document — a
  *scoping* defect in the same file, with the opposite polarity (too broad rather than too early).
- `fragments-new-collection-dialog-enter-never-submits-nno` is another unreachable code path, but
  in the "New collection" dialog: `form?.requestSubmit()` with no `<form>` ancestor. Here the code
  path is reachable and correctly written; it is called **too early**, before its receiver exists.
- `br search` for "new fragment command", "command palette no-op", "shell handle",
  "openAndCreate", "useEffect flush" and "createRoot race" return 0 issues.
